**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 29, verses 1–11:**

It is Meccan. It has 4,195 letters, 1,981 words, and 69 verses.

We were informed by al-Khabbari [in the Isfahan manuscript: Abu al-Husayn al-Khabbari], who said: We were informed by Ibn Hayyan, who said: We were informed by Muhammad ibn Ali al-Farqadi, who said:

We were told by Isma'il ibn Amr, who said: We were told by Yusuf ibn Atiyya, who said: We were told by Harun ibn Kathir, who said: We were told by Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Ankabut will have ten good deeds recorded for him for every believer and hypocrite." [138] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/5.]]

**In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.**

*Alif, Lam, Mim.* 

*Did people think* (ahasiba, "to think, to suppose," which is derived from *hisab*, "reckoning") *that they would be left* (yut-raku) *without being tested or tried, by saying, "We believe"?* This refers to those among the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) who were distressed by the harm of the polytheists. *Nay, We will certainly test them, so that We may distinguish the truthful from the liars.*

The first *an* (that) in *an yut-raku* is in the accusative governed by *ahasiba*, and the second *an* (in *an yaqulu*) is in the genitive by omission of the preposition, meaning *li-anna yaqulu* ("because they say"). The Arabs do not say *tarakto fulanan an yadhhab* ("I left so-and-so that he should go"); they say *tarakto yadhhabu* ("I left him going"). The construction has two possible readings. The first is that the verb *yut-raku* governs *an yaqulu*, meaning "that they be left, [on account of] their saying." The second is a repetition (*taksir*) with the sense: "Did people think that they would be left? Did they think that they would say, 'We believe,' while they are not tried?" [In the Isfahan manuscript: *an yutraku an yaqulu amanna*.] *They are not tried* means they are not tested, so that the sincere can be distinguished from the hypocrite. It is also said that *yuftanun* means they are afflicted by the hardships of this world, meaning that the affliction is not averted from them in this world because they say, "We believe."

The scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse. Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Umayr said: It was revealed concerning Ammar ibn Yasir, when he was tortured for God's sake.

Al-Sha'bi said: These two verses were revealed concerning some people in Mecca who had professed Islam. The Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in Medina wrote to them: "Your profession of Islam will not be accepted until you emigrate." So they set out to return to Medina, but the polytheists pursued them and turned them back. Then this verse was revealed concerning them. They wrote to them: "A verse has been revealed about you, such and such." They said: "We will go out, and if anyone pursues us, we will fight him." So they went out, the polytheists pursued them, and they fought them. Some of them were killed and some escaped. God, glorified is He, then revealed these two verses concerning them.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Mihja' ibn Abd Allah, the freedman of Umar ibn al-Khattab. He was the first to be killed on the day of Badr, when Amir ibn al-Hadrami struck him with an arrow and killed him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On that day, Mihja' is the master of the martyrs, and he is the first of this community to be called to the gate of Paradise." [139] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/324.]] His parents and his wife grieved over him, so God revealed this verse concerning them.

He informed them that they would certainly face affliction and hardship for the sake of God, the Exalted. It is also said that *wa hum la yuftanun* means they are tested through commands and prohibitions.

Then He consoled them, saying, Mighty is He Who speaks: *And We did test those before them, so God will surely make known those who are truthful, and He will surely make known the liars.* God, the Exalted, knows them before the test, and His knowledge is eternal and complete. The meaning of this is: God, the Exalted, will make manifest that (their truthfulness or falsehood) until it becomes existent as known.

Muqatil said: *fa-la-ya'lamanna Allah* means "God will show" (*fa-liyarayanna Allah*). Al-Akhfash said it means "God will distinguish" (*fa-liyumayyizanna Allah*).

Al-Qutaybi said: God's knowledge (*'ilm*) is of two kinds. The first is knowledge of a thing that is known to have occurred. The second is knowledge of a thing that will occur: He knows that it will occur at a certain time, but He does not know it as an actual event until after it has come about and taken place. The proof of this is His saying, *And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and who are steadfast* [[Surat Muhammad: 31.]], meaning: until We know the strivers among you as strivers, and the steadfast as steadfast. Likewise here, *God will surely know that (truth) as existent and occurring*, and this is the way of God's knowledge concerning the future.

*Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us?* That is, *the polytheism* [In the Isfahan manuscript: *i.e., the evil*]. *That they can outrun Us*, meaning *that they can overpower Us* and *say what is in their hearts*, so that He is unable to take vengeance on them. *Evil is their judgment*, meaning: evil is the judgment they pass.

*Whoever hopes for the meeting with God*: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: whoever fears the Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: whoever desires the reward of God. *Then the term of God is surely coming*, meaning what God has promised of reward and punishment, which will certainly occur. *And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.*

*And whoever strives, strives only for his own soul*: he will have its reward. *Indeed, God is Free of need from the worlds.*

*And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove their evil deeds from them and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do*, meaning: with the best of their deeds, which is obedience.

*And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.* The grammarians differed about the reason for the accusative of *husnan*. The people of Basra said: it is by repetition (*al-takrir*), and the sense is *wa-wassaynahu husnan*, meaning "We enjoined him with goodness" (*bi-l-husn*), just as one says *wassaytuhu khayran* ("I enjoined him with good"), meaning *bi-khayr*. The people of Kufa said: the meaning is "We enjoined man that he do good" (*an yaf'ala husnan*), and the verb is omitted because the context indicates it, as in the verse of the rajaz poet:

*"I was amazed at Dahma'*, when they complained against us,
*And at the father of Dahma'*, when he enjoined us
*Good with her, as though we had wronged her."*

That is, he enjoins us to do good to her. This is like His saying, *So he began to wipe* [[Surah Sad: 33.]], meaning "he wipes, wiping."

It is also said that the meaning is: "and We bound him to goodness" (*wa-alzamnahu husnan*).

The majority read *husnan* with a *damma* on the *ha'* and a sukun on the *sin*. Abu Raja' al-Utaridi read it with a *fatha* on both the *ha'* and the *sin*.

In the codex of Ubayy, the reading is *ihsanan* ("kindness"). It was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas al-Zuhri. The name of Abu Waqqas was Malik ibn Wuhayb. When he embraced Islam, his mother Jumna bint Abi Sufyan ibn Umayya ibn Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf said to him: "O Sa'd, I have heard that you have turned away (from our religion). By God, the roof of a house will not shade me, and I will neither eat nor drink, until you disbelieve in Muhammad and return to what you were upon." She was his dearest child to her. Sa'd refused, and she remained for three days without eating, drinking, or seeking shade. Sa'd came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and complained to him about this, so God revealed this verse, along with the one in Luqman and the one in al-Ahqaf. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded him to be gentle with her, to treat her kindly, and not to obey her in polytheism. This is His saying: *And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.*

We were informed by Abd Allah ibn Hamid, by recitation, who said: We were informed by Makki ibn Abdan, who said: We were told by Abd Allah ibn Hashim, who said: We were told by Abu Usama, who said: We were told by Numayr ibn Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I said: "O Messenger of God, who is most deserving of my kindness?" He said: "Your mother." I said: "Then who?" He said: "Your mother." I said: "Then who?" He said: "Your mother." I said: "Then who?" He said: "Then your father, then the nearest, then the nearest." [140] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/3.]]

We were informed by Abd Allah [in the Isfahan manuscript: Abd Allah ibn Hamid, by license from Uthman ibn Ahmad] by license, who said: We were informed by Uthman ibn Ahmad, who said: We were told by Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Wasiti, who said: We were told by Mansur ibn Muhajir, who said: We were told by Abu al-Nadr al-Abbar, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Paradise lies beneath the feet of mothers." [141] [[al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/563.]]

*And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely admit them among the righteous*, meaning among their company and assembly. Muhammad ibn Jarir said: that is, into the place of the righteous, which is Paradise. It is also said that *fi* here means *ma'a* ("with"). The righteous are the saints (*awliya'*) and the prophets.

*And among people is he who says, "We believe in God," but when he is harmed for the sake of God, he takes the trial of people* (their harm and enmity) *as equal to the punishment of God* (in the Hereafter), *and he turns back from his faith. And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say*, meaning those apostates, *"Indeed, we were with you,"* but they are liars. *Is not God most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds? And God will surely make known those who believe, and He will surely make known the hypocrites*, meaning: He will distinguish them and make their condition manifest through trial, test, tribulation, and ordeal.

The exegetes differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse.

Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning people who professed belief with their tongues, but when a calamity from God and an affliction upon their persons befell them, they were tempted (to apostasy). Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning some hypocrites in Mecca who professed belief, but when they were harmed, they returned to polytheism. Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, said: It was revealed concerning the believers whom the polytheists took out with them to Badr, and they apostatized. These are the ones concerning whom He revealed *Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves* [[Surat al-Nisa': 97.]] ... the verse; and the story has already passed. Qatada said: This verse was revealed concerning the people whom the polytheists returned to Mecca.

These ten verses are Medinan up to this point, and the rest of the surah is Meccan.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a ibn al-Mughira ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn Makhzum al-Qurashi. He embraced Islam, and his household frightened him, so he emigrated to Medina before the Prophet (ﷺ) emigrated. His mother, Asma' bint Makhrama ibn Abi Jandal ibn Nahshal al-Tamimi, swore that she would neither eat nor drink, nor wash her head, nor enter a house, until he returned to her. When his two sons, Abu Jahl and al-Harith (the sons of Hisham, who were the maternal brothers of Ayyash), saw her distress and her oath, they went out at night in secret, until they reached Medina and found him. Abu Jahl said to his brother Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a: "You know that you are dearer to your mother than all her children, and you have been dutiful to her. Your mother has sworn that she will neither eat nor drink, nor wash her head, nor enter a house, until you return to her. You claim that your religion enjoins dutifulness to parents. So return to her, for the Lord you worship in Medina is the same Lord in Mecca, so worship Him there." They kept at him until they took from him covenants that they would not oppress him or turn him away from his religion. He gave them the covenants they asked for, and he followed them. His mother had been patient for three days, then she ate and drank. They said: When they had left Medina, the two of them seized him, bound him, and each of them flogged him one hundred lashes, until he renounced the religion of Muhammad (may God have mercy on them both), out of distress from the beating, and he said what was not appropriate. So God revealed concerning him: *And among people is he who says, "We believe in God," but when he is harmed for the sake of God...* the verse.

They said: al-Harith was the harsher of the two against him and the worse in speech. So Ayyash swore by God that if he got him outside the sacred precinct (al-haram), he would strike off his neck. When they returned to Mecca, they stayed for some time. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers emigrated to Medina. Ayyash emigrated, embraced Islam, and his Islam was good.

Then God, the Exalted, cast faith into the heart of al-Harith ibn Hisham. He emigrated to Medina, pledged allegiance to the Prophet (ﷺ) upon Islam, and Ayyash was not present. One day Ayyash met him at the outskirts of Quba', not knowing that he had embraced Islam, and struck off his neck. He was told: "The man had embraced Islam." Ayyash said "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un" and wept. Then he went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of this. So God, the Exalted and Glorified, revealed: *It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake...* the verse.

We were told by Isma'il ibn Amr, who said: We were told by Yusuf ibn Atiyya, who said: We were told by Harun ibn Kathir, who said: We were told by Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Ankabut will have ten good deeds recorded for him for every believer and hypocrite." [138] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/5.]]

**In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.**

*Alif, Lam, Mim.* 

*Did people think* (ahasiba, "to think, to suppose," which is derived from *hisab*, "reckoning") *that they would be left* (yut-raku) *without being tested or tried, by saying, "We believe"?* This refers to those among the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) who were distressed by the harm of the polytheists. *Nay, We will certainly test them, so that We may distinguish the truthful from the liars.*

The first *an* (that) in *an yut-raku* is in the accusative governed by *ahasiba*, and the second *an* (in *an yaqulu*) is in the genitive by omission of the preposition, meaning *li-anna yaqulu* ("because they say"). The Arabs do not say *tarakto fulanan an yadhhab* ("I left so-and-so that he should go"); they say *tarakto yadhhabu* ("I left him going"). The construction has two possible readings. The first is that the verb *yut-raku* governs *an yaqulu*, meaning "that they be left, [on account of] their saying." The second is a repetition (*taksir*) with the sense: "Did people think that they would be left? Did they think that they would say, 'We believe,' while they are not tried?" [In the Isfahan manuscript: *an yutraku an yaqulu amanna*.] *They are not tried* means they are not tested, so that the sincere can be distinguished from the hypocrite. It is also said that *yuftanun* means they are afflicted by the hardships of this world, meaning that the affliction is not averted from them in this world because they say, "We believe."

The scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse. Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Umayr said: It was revealed concerning Ammar ibn Yasir, when he was tortured for God's sake.

Al-Sha'bi said: These two verses were revealed concerning some people in Mecca who had professed Islam. The Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in Medina wrote to them: "Your profession of Islam will not be accepted until you emigrate." So they set out to return to Medina, but the polytheists pursued them and turned them back. Then this verse was revealed concerning them. They wrote to them: "A verse has been revealed about you, such and such." They said: "We will go out, and if anyone pursues us, we will fight him." So they went out, the polytheists pursued them, and they fought them. Some of them were killed and some escaped. God, glorified is He, then revealed these two verses concerning them.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Mihja' ibn Abd Allah, the freedman of Umar ibn al-Khattab. He was the first to be killed on the day of Badr, when Amir ibn al-Hadrami struck him with an arrow and killed him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On that day, Mihja' is the master of the martyrs, and he is the first of this community to be called to the gate of Paradise." [139] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/324.]] His parents and his wife grieved over him, so God revealed this verse concerning them.

He informed them that they would certainly face affliction and hardship for the sake of God, the Exalted. It is also said that *wa hum la yuftanun* means they are tested through commands and prohibitions.

Then He consoled them, saying, Mighty is He Who speaks: *And We did test those before them, so God will surely make known those who are truthful, and He will surely make known the liars.* God, the Exalted, knows them before the test, and His knowledge is eternal and complete. The meaning of this is: God, the Exalted, will make manifest that (their truthfulness or falsehood) until it becomes existent as known.

Muqatil said: *fa-la-ya'lamanna Allah* means "God will show" (*fa-liyarayanna Allah*). Al-Akhfash said it means "God will distinguish" (*fa-liyumayyizanna Allah*).

Al-Qutaybi said: God's knowledge (*'ilm*) is of two kinds. The first is knowledge of a thing that is known to have occurred. The second is knowledge of a thing that will occur: He knows that it will occur at a certain time, but He does not know it as an actual event until after it has come about and taken place. The proof of this is His saying, *And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and who are steadfast* [[Surat Muhammad: 31.]], meaning: until We know the strivers among you as strivers, and the steadfast as steadfast. Likewise here, *God will surely know that (truth) as existent and occurring*, and this is the way of God's knowledge concerning the future.

*Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us?* That is, *the polytheism* [In the Isfahan manuscript: *i.e., the evil*]. *That they can outrun Us*, meaning *that they can overpower Us* and *say what is in their hearts*, so that He is unable to take vengeance on them. *Evil is their judgment*, meaning: evil is the judgment they pass.

*Whoever hopes for the meeting with God*: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: whoever fears the Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: whoever desires the reward of God. *Then the term of God is surely coming*, meaning what God has promised of reward and punishment, which will certainly occur. *And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.*

*And whoever strives, strives only for his own soul*: he will have its reward. *Indeed, God is Free of need from the worlds.*

*And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove their evil deeds from them and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do*, meaning: with the best of their deeds, which is obedience.

*And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.* The grammarians differed about the reason for the accusative of *husnan*. The people of Basra said: it is by repetition (*al-takrir*), and the sense is *wa-wassaynahu husnan*, meaning "We enjoined him with goodness" (*bi-l-husn*), just as one says *wassaytuhu khayran* ("I enjoined him with good"), meaning *bi-khayr*. The people of Kufa said: the meaning is "We enjoined man that he do good" (*an yaf'ala husnan*), and the verb is omitted because the context indicates it, as in the verse of the rajaz poet:

*"I was amazed at Dahma'*, when they complained against us,
*And at the father of Dahma'*, when he enjoined us
*Good with her, as though we had wronged her."*

That is, he enjoins us to do good to her. This is like His saying, *So he began to wipe* [[Surah Sad: 33.]], meaning "he wipes, wiping."

It is also said that the meaning is: "and We bound him to goodness" (*wa-alzamnahu husnan*).

The majority read *husnan* with a *damma* on the *ha'* and a sukun on the *sin*. Abu Raja' al-Utaridi read it with a *fatha* on both the *ha'* and the *sin*.

In the codex of Ubayy, the reading is *ihsanan* ("kindness"). It was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas al-Zuhri. The name of Abu Waqqas was Malik ibn Wuhayb. When he embraced Islam, his mother Jumna bint Abi Sufyan ibn Umayya ibn Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf said to him: "O Sa'd, I have heard that you have turned away (from our religion). By God, the roof of a house will not shade me, and I will neither eat nor drink, until you disbelieve in Muhammad and return to what you were upon." She was his dearest child to her. Sa'd refused, and she remained for three days without eating, drinking, or seeking shade. Sa'd came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and complained to him about this, so God revealed this verse, along with the one in Luqman and the one in al-Ahqaf. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded him to be gentle with her, to treat her kindly, and not to obey her in polytheism. This is His saying: *And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.*

We were informed by Abd Allah ibn Hamid, by recitation, who said: We were informed by Makki ibn Abdan, who said: We were told by Abd Allah ibn Hashim, who said: We were told by Abu Usama, who said: We were told by Numayr ibn Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I said: "O Messenger of God, who is most deserving of my kindness?" He said: "Your mother." I said: "Then who?" He said: "Your mother." I said: "Then who?" He said: "Your mother." I said: "Then who?" He said: "Then your father, then the nearest, then the nearest." [140] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/3.]]

We were informed by Abd Allah [in the Isfahan manuscript: Abd Allah ibn Hamid, by license from Uthman ibn Ahmad] by license, who said: We were informed by Uthman ibn Ahmad, who said: We were told by Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Wasiti, who said: We were told by Mansur ibn Muhajir, who said: We were told by Abu al-Nadr al-Abbar, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Paradise lies beneath the feet of mothers." [141] [[al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/563.]]

*And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely admit them among the righteous*, meaning among their company and assembly. Muhammad ibn Jarir said: that is, into the place of the righteous, which is Paradise. It is also said that *fi* here means *ma'a* ("with"). The righteous are the saints (*awliya'*) and the prophets.

*And among people is he who says, "We believe in God," but when he is harmed for the sake of God, he takes the trial of people* (their harm and enmity) *as equal to the punishment of God* (in the Hereafter), *and he turns back from his faith. And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say*, meaning those apostates, *"Indeed, we were with you,"* but they are liars. *Is not God most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds? And God will surely make known those who believe, and He will surely make known the hypocrites*, meaning: He will distinguish them and make their condition manifest through trial, test, tribulation, and ordeal.

The exegetes differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse.

Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning people who professed belief with their tongues, but when a calamity from God and an affliction upon their persons befell them, they were tempted (to apostasy). Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning some hypocrites in Mecca who professed belief, but when they were harmed, they returned to polytheism. Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, said: It was revealed concerning the believers whom the polytheists took out with them to Badr, and they apostatized. These are the ones concerning whom He revealed *Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves* [[Surat al-Nisa': 97.]] ... the verse; and the story has already passed. Qatada said: This verse was revealed concerning the people whom the polytheists returned to Mecca.

These ten verses are Medinan up to this point, and the rest of the surah is Meccan.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a ibn al-Mughira ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn Makhzum al-Qurashi. He embraced Islam, and his household frightened him, so he emigrated to Medina before the Prophet (ﷺ) emigrated. His mother, Asma' bint Makhrama ibn Abi Jandal ibn Nahshal al-Tamimi, swore that she would neither eat nor drink, nor wash her head, nor enter a house, until he returned to her. When his two sons, Abu Jahl and al-Harith (the sons of Hisham, who were the maternal brothers of Ayyash), saw her distress and her oath, they went out at night in secret, until they reached Medina and found him. Abu Jahl said to his brother Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a: "You know that you are dearer to your mother than all her children, and you have been dutiful to her. Your mother has sworn that she will neither eat nor drink, nor wash her head, nor enter a house, until you return to her. You claim that your religion enjoins dutifulness to parents. So return to her, for the Lord you worship in Medina is the same Lord in Mecca, so worship Him there." They kept at him until they took from him covenants that they would not oppress him or turn him away from his religion. He gave them the covenants they asked for, and he followed them. His mother had been patient for three days, then she ate and drank. They said: When they had left Medina, the two of them seized him, bound him, and each of them flogged him one hundred lashes, until he renounced the religion of Muhammad (may God have mercy on them both), out of distress from the beating, and he said what was not appropriate. So God revealed concerning him: *And among people is he who says, "We believe in God," but when he is harmed for the sake of God...* the verse.

They said: al-Harith was the harsher of the two against him and the worse in speech. So Ayyash swore by God that if he got him outside the sacred precinct (al-haram), he would strike off his neck. When they returned to Mecca, they stayed for some time. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers emigrated to Medina. Ayyash emigrated, embraced Islam, and his Islam was good.

Then God, the Exalted, cast faith into the heart of al-Harith ibn Hisham. He emigrated to Medina, pledged allegiance to the Prophet (ﷺ) upon Islam, and Ayyash was not present. One day Ayyash met him at the outskirts of Quba', not knowing that he had embraced Islam, and struck off his neck. He was told: "The man had embraced Islam." Ayyash said "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un" and wept. Then he went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of this. So God, the Exalted and Glorified, revealed: *It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake...* the verse.

﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ Those who disbelieved, from the people of Makkah, said to those who believed: ﴿Follow our way, and we will bear your sins.﴾ Al-Farra' said: The word is in the imperative form, but its meaning is a conditional (jaza'): it means, "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins," like His saying, ﴿فَلْيُلْقِهِ الْيَمُّ بِالسَّاحِلِ﴾ ("Let the sea cast him onto the shore") and His saying, ﴿لا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمانُ وَجُنُودُهُ﴾ ("Let not Solomon and his soldiers crush you"). The word is in the form of a prohibition, but its interpretation is a conditional. A poet said:

*"I said: call, and I will call, for the sweetest sound is when two callers call out."*

He means: "If you call, I will call."

Then Allah refuted them, saying: ﴿وَما هُمْ بِحامِلِينَ مِنْ خَطاياهُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ﴾ "They will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars." ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ﴾ "They will surely bear their own burdens, and burdens along with their burdens," ﴿وَأَثْقالًا مَعَ أَثْقالِهِمْ﴾, which is similar to: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا أَوْزارَهُمْ كامِلَةً يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ وَمِنْ أَوْزارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ "that they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge" [Surah al-Nahl: 25], and so on.

'Awf narrated from al-Hasan that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever calls to guidance, and it is followed and acted upon, he will have a reward like the rewards of those who followed him, without that diminishing anything of their rewards. And whoever calls to misguidance, and it is followed and acted upon, he will have a burden like the burdens of those who followed him, without that diminishing anything of their burdens." [142] [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/142]

Then al-Hasan recited: ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ وَأَثْقالًا مَعَ أَثْقالِهِمْ﴾.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki ibn Abdan informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hashim told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hilal al-'Absi [in one copy: al-'Absi], from Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us and urged us to give charity, but the people were slow, until anger was seen on his face. Then a man from the Ansar stood up, brought a purse and gave it, and the people followed, giving until joy was seen on his face. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever establishes a good practice (sunnah hasanah), he will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it, without that diminishing anything of their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil practice, he will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it, without that diminishing anything of their burdens." [143] [Musnad Ahmad: 4/362]

﴿وَلَيُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ عَمَّا كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ "And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate." ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عاماً فَأَخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفانُ وَهُمْ ظالِمُونَ﴾ "And We sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers."

Ibn 'Abbas said: Noah (peace be upon him) was sent at the age of forty, and he remained among his people calling them for a thousand years less fifty years. He lived after the flood sixty years, until the people multiplied and spread.

﴿فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَأَصْحابَ السَّفِينَةِ وَجَعَلْناها آيَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ "So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and made it a sign for the worlds." ﴿وَإِبْراهِيمَ إِذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ "And Abraham, when he said to his people: Worship Allah and fear Him; that is better for you, if you knew. ﴿إِنَّما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثاناً وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً﴾ "You only worship idols other than Allah, and you invent a lie."

They say falsely. Mujahid said: "You make idols with your hands, then you call them gods." A similar verse is His saying: ﴿أَتَعْبُدُونَ ما تَنْحِتُونَ﴾ "Do you worship what you carve?" [Surah al-Saffat: 95]. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami recited ﴿وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً﴾ with the emphatic and intensive form (al-mubalaghah wa al-kathrah).

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لا يَمْلِكُونَ لَكُمْ رِزْقاً فَابْتَغُوا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الرِّزْقَ وَاعْبُدُوهُ وَاشْكُرُوا لَهُ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ "Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision; so seek provision from Allah, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned." ﴿وَإِنْ تُكَذِّبُوا فَقَدْ كَذَّبَ أُمَمٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ فاهلكوا وَما عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ﴾ "And if you deny, then nations before you denied, and the Messenger has only the clear conveyance."

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾ with the ta' (تاء, "they have not seen" addressed as "you") is the reading of the Kufans, and the others read it with the ya' (ياء). ﴿كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ﴾ "Have they not seen how Allah originates creation, then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah." ﴿قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ﴾ "Say: Travel in the earth and observe how He originated creation." It means: look at the dwellings, homes and remains of the past generations, and how He began their creation. Nothing was difficult for Him in originating it, so likewise it is not difficult for Him to bring it back again.

﴿ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ﴾ "Then Allah produces the final creation," meaning He begins the final beginning after death.

There are two forms of this word: *nash'ah* with the long vowel (al-mad), which is the recitation of Ibn Kathir, al-Hasan, Abu 'Amr and Habib, and *nash'ah* with the short vowel and a sukun on the sin, which is the recitation of the people [in the Isfahan copy: the rest]. Its parallel is *al-ra'fah* (kindness) [so in the manuscript], and *al-ra'fah*, ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ "Indeed, Allah is over all things competent. ﴿يُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَرْحَمُ مَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ تُقْلَبُونَ﴾ and to Him you will be returned," meaning you will be brought back and turned over.

﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ Those who disbelieved, from the people of Makkah, said to those who believed: ﴿Follow our way, and we will bear your sins.﴾ Al-Farra' said: The word is in the imperative form, but its meaning is a conditional (jaza'): it means, "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins," like His saying, ﴿فَلْيُلْقِهِ الْيَمُّ بِالسَّاحِلِ﴾ ("Let the sea cast him onto the shore") and His saying, ﴿لا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمانُ وَجُنُودُهُ﴾ ("Let not Solomon and his soldiers crush you"). The word is in the form of a prohibition, but its interpretation is a conditional. A poet said:

*"I said: call, and I will call, for the sweetest sound is when two callers call out."*

He means: "If you call, I will call."

Then Allah refuted them, saying: ﴿وَما هُمْ بِحامِلِينَ مِنْ خَطاياهُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ﴾ "They will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars." ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ﴾ "They will surely bear their own burdens, and burdens along with their burdens," ﴿وَأَثْقالًا مَعَ أَثْقالِهِمْ﴾, which is similar to: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا أَوْزارَهُمْ كامِلَةً يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ وَمِنْ أَوْزارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ "that they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge" [Surah al-Nahl: 25], and so on.

'Awf narrated from al-Hasan that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever calls to guidance, and it is followed and acted upon, he will have a reward like the rewards of those who followed him, without that diminishing anything of their rewards. And whoever calls to misguidance, and it is followed and acted upon, he will have a burden like the burdens of those who followed him, without that diminishing anything of their burdens." [142] [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/142]

Then al-Hasan recited: ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ وَأَثْقالًا مَعَ أَثْقالِهِمْ﴾.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki ibn Abdan informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hashim told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hilal al-'Absi [in one copy: al-'Absi], from Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us and urged us to give charity, but the people were slow, until anger was seen on his face. Then a man from the Ansar stood up, brought a purse and gave it, and the people followed, giving until joy was seen on his face. ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ Those who disbelieved, from the people of Makkah, said to those who believed: ﴿Follow our way, and we will bear your sins.﴾ Al-Farra' said: The word is in the imperative form, but its meaning is a conditional (jaza'): it means, "If you follow our way, we will bear your sins," like His saying, ﴿فَلْيُلْقِهِ الْيَمُّ بِالسَّاحِلِ﴾ ("Let the sea cast him onto the shore") and His saying, ﴿لا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمانُ وَجُنُودُهُ﴾ ("Let not Solomon and his soldiers crush you"). The word is in the form of a prohibition, but its interpretation is a conditional. A poet said:

*"I said: call, and I will call, for the sweetest sound is when two callers call out."*

He means: "If you call, I will call."

Then Allah refuted them, saying: ﴿وَما هُمْ بِحامِلِينَ مِنْ خَطاياهُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ﴾ "They will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars." ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ﴾ "They will surely bear their own burdens, and burdens along with their burdens," ﴿وَأَثْقالًا مَعَ أَثْقالِهِمْ﴾, which is similar to: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا أَوْزارَهُمْ كامِلَةً يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ وَمِنْ أَوْزارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ "that they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge" [Surah al-Nahl: 25], and so on.

'Awf narrated from al-Hasan that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever calls to guidance, and it is followed and acted upon, he will have a reward like the rewards of those who followed him, without that diminishing anything of their rewards. And whoever calls to misguidance, and it is followed and acted upon, he will have a burden like the burdens of those who followed him, without that diminishing anything of their burdens." [142] [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/142]

Then al-Hasan recited: ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ وَأَثْقالًا مَعَ أَثْقالِهِمْ﴾.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki ibn Abdan informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hashim told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hilal al-'Absi [in one copy: al-'Absi], from Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us and urged us to give charity, but the people were slow, until anger was seen on his face. Then a man from the Ansar stood up, brought a purse and gave it, and the people followed, giving until joy was seen on his face. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever establishes a good practice (sunnah hasanah), he will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it, without that diminishing anything of their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil practice, he will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it, without that diminishing anything of their burdens." [143] [Musnad Ahmad: 4/362]

﴿وَلَيُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ عَمَّا كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ "And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate." ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عاماً فَأَخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفانُ وَهُمْ ظالِمُونَ﴾ "And We sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers."

Ibn 'Abbas said: Noah (peace be upon him) was sent at the age of forty, and he remained among his people calling them for a thousand years less fifty years. He lived after the flood sixty years, until the people multiplied and spread.

﴿فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَأَصْحابَ السَّفِينَةِ وَجَعَلْناها آيَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ "So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and made it a sign for the worlds." ﴿وَإِبْراهِيمَ إِذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ "And Abraham, when he said to his people: Worship Allah and fear Him; that is better for you, if you knew. ﴿إِنَّما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثاناً وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً﴾ "You only worship idols other than Allah, and you invent a lie."

They say falsely. Mujahid said: "You make idols with your hands, then you call them gods." A similar verse is His saying: ﴿أَتَعْبُدُونَ ما تَنْحِتُونَ﴾ "Do you worship what you carve?" [Surah al-Saffat: 95]. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami recited ﴿وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً﴾ with the emphatic and intensive form (al-mubalaghah wa al-kathrah).

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لا يَمْلِكُونَ لَكُمْ رِزْقاً فَابْتَغُوا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الرِّزْقَ وَاعْبُدُوهُ وَاشْكُرُوا لَهُ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ "Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision; so seek provision from Allah, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned." ﴿وَإِنْ تُكَذِّبُوا فَقَدْ كَذَّبَ أُمَمٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ فاهلكوا وَما عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ﴾ "And if you deny, then nations before you denied, and the Messenger has only the clear conveyance."

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾ with the ta' (تاء, "they have not seen" addressed as "you") is the reading of the Kufans, and the others read it with the ya' (ياء). ﴿كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ﴾ "Have they not seen how Allah originates creation, then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah." ﴿قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ﴾ "Say: Travel in the earth and observe how He originated creation." It means: look at the dwellings, homes and remains of the past generations, and how He began their creation. Nothing was difficult for Him in originating it, so likewise it is not difficult for Him to bring it back again.

﴿ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ﴾ "Then Allah produces the final creation," meaning He begins the final beginning after death.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 29, verse 22–27:

﴿And you cannot escape [Allah] on earth or in the heaven.﴾ The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) differed over its interpretation. Al-Farra' said: its meaning is "nor is whoever is in the heaven incapable [of overpowering you]," and this is from the obscure points of Arabic grammar: the pronoun that is not expressed in the second part. Like the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit:

"So whoever among you satirises the Messenger of Allah, and whoever praises him and supports him, are equal." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/337; al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/356, where it reads "amman" instead of "faman".]

He meant: "and whoever praises him and supports him," so he omitted "man" and what it refers to. To this interpretation Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd also went, saying: "The people of the earth cannot overpower [Allah] on the earth, nor the people of the heaven in the heaven, if they disobey."

Qutrub said: "nor in the heaven if you were in it," like your saying: "So-and-so does not escape me in Basra, nor here in my town," while he is with you in the town; i.e., nor in Basra if he went there.

﴿And you have no protector or helper besides Allah.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and His meeting—those have despaired of My mercy, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ Thus He, glorified is He, turned with these verses to admonish and warn the people of Mecca. Then He returned to the story of Abraham, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:

﴿So the answer of his people was not but that they said, "Kill him or burn him."﴾ The common readers recite "jawaba" with a fatha on the ba' as the predicate of kana, and "an qalu" is in the position of the nominative as the subject of kana. Salim al-Aftas recited "jawabu" with a damma as the subject of kana, and "an" then occupies the accusative position as its predicate.

﴿But Allah saved him from the fire.﴾ He made it cool and safe for him. Ka'b said: "What was burned of him was only his bonds."

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ And he (peace be upon him) said to his people—meaning Abraham (peace be upon him):

﴿Indeed you have taken, other than Allah, idols as a means of affection among you in worldly life.﴾ The readers differed over it. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub recited "mawaddatu" with a damma and "baynikum" with a kasra as an annexation (idafa), and this was preferred by Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim, in the sense that: the idols you have taken other than Allah are the affection among you in the life of this world, which has not been severed, and which will not benefit in the Hereafter. Like His saying: [﴿They did not remain but an hour of a day﴾, then He said: ﴿a proclamation﴾] [Surah al-Ahqaf: 35], i.e., this is a proclamation; and His saying, glorified is He: [﴿They will not succeed﴾, then He said: ﴿enjoyment﴾] [Surah Yunus: 69–70], i.e., it is enjoyment. Likewise, they here omitted "hiya" (it). It is also permissible that it be the predicate of "inna."

Asim, in some transmissions, recited "mawaddatun" with a damma and tanwin and "baynakum" with a fatha, which returns to the meaning of the first reading. Hamza recited "mawadata" with a fatha and "baynikum" with a kasra as an annexation, the unity (ittihad) falling upon it, and he treated "innama" as a single particle; this is the transmission of Hafs from Asim. The others recited "mawadatan" with a fatha and tanwin and "baynakum" with a fatha, which returns to Hamza's reading. The meaning of the verse is that you have taken these idols as affection among you in the life of this world.

﴿Affection among you in the life of this world﴾: you show affection to one another and love one another over their worship, and you associate with one another through it.

﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disavow others, and some of you will curse others,﴾ and the idols will disown their worshippers. ﴿And your refuge will be the Fire, all of you—the worshippers and the worshipped—﴿ ﴿and you will have no helpers.﴾ ﴿So Lot believed him,﴾ and he was the first to affirm Abraham (peace be upon him) when he saw that the fire had not harmed him.

﴿And he said, "Indeed I am emigrating to my Lord.﴾ He emigrated from Kuwa—from the countryside of Kufa—to Harran, then to the Levant, accompanied by his nephew Lot and his wife Sarah, and he was the first to emigrate. Muqatil said: Abraham (peace be upon him) emigrated when he was seventy-five years old.

﴿Indeed He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and We placed in his descendants prophethood and the Scripture, and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 29, verses 28–35:**

﴿And Lot, when he said to his people: "Indeed, you commit an abomination that no one among the worlds has preceded you in. Do you indeed approach men, and cut off the road, and commit the evil in your gathering?"﴾

Abu al-'Abbas Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi narrated to us, saying: My maternal grandfather Abu al-Hasan al-Mahmudi narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzayma informed us that Bishr ibn Mu'adh al-'Aqadi narrated to them, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us [in the copy of Isfahan: "Bara'"], saying: Hatim ibn Abi Saghira narrated to us. And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba narrated to us, saying: 'Umayr ibn Mirdas al-Dawniqi narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi narrated to us, saying:

Yahya ibn Abi al-Hajjaj Abu Ayyub al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Abu Yunus Hatim ibn Abi Saghira narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Abu Mawla Umm Hani, from Umm Hani bint Abi Talib, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about His saying, ﴿and commit the evil in your gathering﴾. I said: "What is the evil that they used to commit?"

He said: "They used to pelt (khadhf) the people of the roads and mock them."

And al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiyya narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyab narrated to us, saying: I heard Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad narrating from Mu'awiya, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the people of Lot used to sit in their assemblies, and beside every man among them was a bowl containing pebbles. Whenever a passerby came by them, they would pelt him, and whichever of them struck him, he had the right to him." And this is the saying of Allah, ﴿and commit the evil in your gathering﴾.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of khadhf, for it does not wound the enemy, nor does it hit game, but it gouges out the eye and breaks the tooth."

And al-Husayn informed us, saying: Abu 'Ali ibn Hunays al-Muqri' informed us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Muqri' narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Husayn al-Kisa'i narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Hatim narrated to us, saying:

Abu Bakr ibn Aws al-Madani informed us, from his father, from Yazid ibn Bakr ibn Da'b, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, regarding ﴿and commit the evil in your gathering﴾, he said: "The breaking of wind (dhara't); they used to break wind in their assemblies." And Mujahid said: "Some of them used to have intercourse with one another in their assemblies."

Abu Ja'far al-Khalfani informed us, saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Tabbani [in the copy of Isfahan: "al-Tabban"] narrated to us, saying: Abu Labid [in the copy of Isfahan: "Lunayd"] al-Sarakhsi narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Umar ibn Shafiq narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Zarif narrated to us, from Makhul, who said: "Ten of the traits of the people of Lot are found in this Community: chewing gum (mudgh al-'ilk), dyeing the fingers with henna (tatwiq al-asabi' bil-hina'), untying the waist-wrap (hall al-izar), trimming the fingers, the turban wrapped around the head, al-salīnīya [in the copy of Isfahan: "al-sakina"], throwing the slingshot (ramy al-julahiq), whistling (al-safir), pelting (al-khadhf), and sodomy (al-lutiyya)."

﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said: "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are of the truthful."﴾ Indeed, it is coming upon them, for he had threatened them with the punishment. ﴿He said: "My Lord, help me against the corrupting people."﴾

﴿And when Our messengers came to Abraham with glad tidings﴾ from Allah, the Exalted, of Isaac and Jacob: ﴿they said: "Indeed, we will destroy the people of this town"﴾, meaning the people of Lot, ﴿"indeed its people have been wrongdoers."﴾ Abraham said to the messengers: ﴿"Indeed, Lot is in it."﴾ They said: ﴿"We are most knowing of who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she is of those who remain behind."﴾

﴿And when Our messengers came to Lot﴾, and he supposed that they were of mankind, ﴿he was distressed for them and felt helplessness regarding them. They said: "Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is of those who remain behind. Indeed, we will send down upon the people of this town a punishment (rijz), a torment from the sky, because they have been defiantly disobedient."﴾

﴿And We have left of it a clear sign﴾, a manifest lesson ﴿for a people who reason.﴾ It is the report of what was done to them. And Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the remaining traces of their dwellings, in ruin. Abu al-'Aliya and Qatada said: it is the stones which Allah cast down. Mujahid said: it is the black water upon the surface of the earth.

Abu Ja'far al-Khalfani informed us, saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Tabbani [in the copy of Isfahan: "al-Tabban"] narrated to us, saying: Abu Labid [in the copy of Isfahan: "Lunayd"] al-Sarakhsi narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Umar ibn Shafiq narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Zarif narrated to us, from Makhul, who said: "Ten of the traits of the people of Lot are found in this Community: chewing gum (mudgh al-'ilk), dyeing the fingers with henna (tatwiq al-asabi' bil-hina'), untying the waist-wrap (hall al-izar), trimming the fingers, the turban wrapped around the head, al-salīnīya [in the copy of Isfahan: "al-sakina"], throwing the slingshot (ramy al-julahiq), whistling (al-safir), pelting (al-khadhf), and sodomy (al-lutiyya)."

﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said: "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are of the truthful."﴾ Indeed, it is coming upon them, for he had threatened them with the punishment. ﴿He said: "My Lord, help me against the corrupting people."﴾

﴿And when Our messengers came to Abraham with glad tidings﴾ from Allah, the Exalted, of Isaac and Jacob: ﴿they said: "Indeed, we will destroy the people of this town"﴾, meaning the people of Lot, ﴿"indeed its people have been wrongdoers."﴾ Abraham said to the messengers: ﴿"Indeed, Lot is in it."﴾ They said: ﴿"We are most knowing of who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she is of those who remain behind."﴾

﴿And when Our messengers came to Lot﴾, and he supposed that they were of mankind, ﴿he was distressed for them and felt helplessness regarding them. They said: "Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is of those who remain behind. Indeed, we will send down upon the people of this town a punishment (rijz), a torment from the sky, because they have been defiantly disobedient."﴾

﴿And We have left of it a clear sign﴾, a manifest lesson ﴿for a people who reason.﴾ It is the report of what was done to them. And Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the remaining traces of their dwellings, in ruin. Abu al-'Aliya and Qatada said: it is the stones which Allah cast down. Mujahid said: it is the black water upon the surface of the earth.

And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb, and he said: "O my people, worship Allah and hope for the Last Day, and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief." But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became prostrate in their homes. And [We destroyed] 'Ad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their dwellings. Satan made their deeds appear fair to them and barred them from the way, though they were discerning [people].

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 29, verses 41–45:**

﴿The likeness of those who take protectors besides Allah﴾, that is, the idols, "who hope for their help and benefit when they are in need of them, is like the spider's, which takes a house for itself so that it may shelter it, but its building does not avail it anything when it needs it." Just as the spider's house does not keep off cold or heat, so these idols possess no power to benefit or harm their worshippers, neither good nor evil.

﴿And indeed the frailest of houses is the spider's house, if only they knew.﴾ The grammarians said: *al-'Ankabut* (the spider) is feminine by the *ta'* in it, though some Arabs make it masculine. Al-Farra' recited:

*"Over their rainfall, among them, are houses… as if the spider were the one who built them."* [[In the Isfahan copy: "منها" (among them) instead of "منهم".]] [[Lisan al-'Arab: 1/632.]]

Its measure (*wazn*) is *fa'lalun*.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba related to us, saying: Abu Hamid al-Mustamli related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Dabbi related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Makki related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah related to me, saying: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad say: I heard my father say: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said:

"Purify your houses from spiderwebs, for leaving them in the houses brings poverty."

He said: I heard 'Ali say:

"Withholding leaven brings poverty."

﴿Indeed Allah knows what they call upon besides Him, of anything.﴾ [The verb "yad'una" is read with the *ya'* by the people of Basra, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading, saying: because the nations before them are mentioned.]

On the reading of this word, there is a difference reported from 'Asim: others read it with the *ta'* ("tad'una").

﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ ﴿And these are the parables, which We strike for mankind; but none understands them except the learned.﴾ "Al-Amthal" means things and attributes. A *mathal* (parable) is a saying that compares the state of the second to the first. "Nadribuha" means: We clarify them. "Li-l-nas" means: for people.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Manda [[In the Isfahan copy: Ibn Barzah.]] related to us, saying: al-Harith [[In the Isfahan copy: al-Harith.]] ibn Abi Usama related to us, saying: Dawud ibn al-Mukhbir related to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Kathir related to us, from Abu Jurayj [[In the Isfahan copy: Jurayj.]], from 'Ata' and Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse: "And these are the parables We strike for mankind; but none understands them except the learned," and said: "The learned is the one who understands from Allah and acts in obedience to Him and avoids His wrath." [147] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/346.]]

﴿Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth. Indeed in that is a sign for the believers.﴾ ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book, and establish the prayer. Indeed, the prayer forbids indecency and wrongdoing.﴾

Ibn 'Umar said: "It suffices" (*tughni*). Al-Farra' said: that it forbids (*an tanha*) indecency and wrongdoing. The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿And do not raise your voice in your prayer﴾, meaning your recitation. Others said: it is the prayer that includes bowing and prostration.

Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas said: in the prayer there is a limit and a restraint from disobedience to Allah, the Exalted. Whoever is not commanded by his prayer to do good and forbidden from evil, his prayer increases him in distance from Allah and nothing more.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no prayer for one who does not obey the prayer, and obedience to the prayer is that it forbids indecency and wrongdoing." [148] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/146.]]

Abu Sufyan related from Jabir, who said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "So-and-so prays by day and steals by night." He said: "Indeed his prayer will restrain him." [149] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/29.]]

Anas ibn Malik said: A young man from the Ansar used to pray the prayers [In the Isfahan copy: "the prayers".] with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then he would not leave any indecency without committing it. His condition was described to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and he said: "Indeed his prayer will restrain him one day." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/348.]] He did not delay before he repented and his condition improved. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Did I not tell you that his prayer would restrain him one day?" [150]

Ibn 'Awn said: its meaning is that the prayer restrains its performer from indecency and wrongdoing for as long as he is in it. The people of meanings (*ahl al-ma'ani*) said: his prayer should restrain him, like His saying: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾. [[Surah Al 'Imran: 97.]]

﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater.﴾ Scholars differed in its interpretation. Some said: its meaning is that Allah's remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. This is the view of 'Abd Allah, Salman, Mujahid, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and a report of 'Abd Allah ibn Rabi'ah from Ibn 'Abbas. This was also related as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report:

We were informed by al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Dinawari, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abi Dawud al-Bazki related to us, saying: al-Husayn al-Lahbani related to us, saying: Salih ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwa related to us, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Uqbah, from his paternal uncle Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, "Allah's remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 20/190.]] [151]

The wise said: because Allah's remembrance of the servant is on the level of independence (*istighna'*), and the servant's remembrance of Him is on the level of need (*iftiqar*). Also, His remembrance is continuous, while the servant's remembrance is temporary. Also, the servant's remembrance is for the removal or repulsion of harm, while Allah's remembrance of him is for grace and generosity. Dhu al-Nun said: because you remembered Him after He remembered you. Ibn 'Ata' said: because His remembrance of you is without cause, while your remembrance is mixed with causes. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: because His remembrance of the servant freed his tongue to remember Him, and because the servant's remembrance is created while His remembrance is uncreated.

Abu al-Darda', Ibn Zayd and Qatadah said: its meaning is ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ than anything else, and it is the best of everything.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi al-Hafiz informed me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Ya'qub al-Maqdisi related to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning His words: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾: "The remembrance of Allah in every state is better and more excellent, and the remembrance is that we remember Him when He has forbidden something, so we leave what He has forbidden, and we remember Him when He has permitted something, so we take what He has permitted." [152]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad [In the Isfahan copy: from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad.] informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Furbani related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi informed us, saying: I heard Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Zaydi narrate to my father 'Abd Allah al-Qarraz, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: While we were travelling with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Hamdan with a drum, he [the Prophet] became alert, and said [In the Isfahan copy: "He said: O Mu'adh, where are the foremost ones?" I said: "They have gone ahead, and some people have lagged behind." He said: "O Mu'adh, indeed the foremost…" etc.]: "O Mu'adh, indeed the foremost are those who are absorbed in the remembrance of Allah. Whoever wishes to graze in the gardens of Paradise, let him increase his remembrance of Allah, the Exalted." [153] [[Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah: 7/72; and Al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/205.]]

Ishaq ibn Sulayman said: I heard Hariz ibn 'Uthman narrate [[In Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' (1/455), from al-Mashyakhah, from Abu Bahriyyah.]] from Abu Bahriyyah, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: No son of Adam has done a deed that saves him more from the punishment of Allah than the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted. They said: "Not even fighting in the way of Allah?" He said: "No, even if he strikes with his sword." [[In al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (3/5), from Jabir, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), and at its end: "unless you strike with your sword."]] Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Furbani related to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Ammar al-Mus'abi related to us, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Salih ibn Abi Gharib, from Kathir ibn Murrah al-Hadrami, who said: I heard Abu al-Darda' say: "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the most beloved to your King, the most perfect in your ranks, and better for you than that you should fight your enemy and they strike your necks and you strike theirs, and better than giving gold and silver?" They said: "What is it, O Abu al-Darda'?" He said: "The remembrance of Allah." Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾.

It was said to Salman: "Which deed is best?" He said: "Do you not read the Qur'an: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾? Nothing is better than the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted."

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Humayd ibn Dawud related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Khalid related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit related to us, from his father, from Makhul, from Jubayr ibn Hubayr [In the Isfahan copy: Nafir.], from Malik ibn 'Amir, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Which deeds are most beloved to Allah, the Exalted?"

He (ﷺ) said: "That you die while your tongue is moist with the remembrance of Allah." [154] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 1/414, no. 1752.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Salamah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Mujashi' al-Bahili related to us, saying: Khalid ibn Yazid al-'Umari related to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri related to us, from 'Ata' ibn Qurrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Damrah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The world is cursed, and what is in it is cursed, except the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and what is associated with it, or a scholar, or a student." [155] [[Fath al-Qadir: 1/8; and Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/185, no. 6085.]]

The wise said: the remembrance is the best of things because the reward of remembrance is remembrance. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you﴾. [[Surah al-Baqarah: 152.]] This is supported by what

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hisham related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am according to My servant's expectation of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs; and if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; and if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running.'" [156] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/413.]]

'Abd Allah informed us, saying: 'Ali informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-A'azz Abu Muslim, who said: I bear witness about Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id that they both testified that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No group sits remembering Allah, the Exalted, except that the angels surround them, mercy covers them, and He mentions them among those who are with Him." [157] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/49.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shaybah related to us, saying: al-Furbani related to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shanba related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, concerning ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾: "The remembrance of Allah of the servant during the prayer is greater than the prayer." Ibn 'Awn said: its meaning is: the prayer you are in, and Allah's remembrance of you in it, is greater than what the prayer has forbidden you from, of indecency and wrongdoing. Ibn 'Ata' said: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ than that you should remain in disobedience while in it.

﴿And Allah knows what you do.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 29, verses 41–45:**

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Furbani related to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Ammar al-Mus'abi related to us, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Salih ibn Abi Gharib, from Kathir ibn Murrah al-Hadrami, who said: I heard Abu al-Darda' say: "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the most beloved to your King, the most perfect in your ranks, and better for you than that you should fight your enemy and they strike your necks and you strike theirs, and better than giving gold and silver?" It was said to Salman: "Which deed is best?" He said: "Do you not read the Qur'an: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾? Nothing is better than the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted."

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Humayd ibn Dawud related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Khalid related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit related to us, from his father, from Makhul, from Jubayr ibn Hubayr [In the Isfahan copy: Nafir.], from Malik ibn 'Amir, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Which deeds are most beloved to Allah, the Exalted?"

[155] [[Fath al-Qadir: 1/8; and Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/185, no. 6085.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hisham related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am according to My servant's expectation of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. [157] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/49.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shaybah related to us, saying: al-Furbani related to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shanba related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, concerning ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾: "The remembrance of Allah of the servant during the prayer is greater than the prayer."
