'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hisham related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am according to My servant's expectation of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs; and if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; and if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running.'" [156] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/413.]]

'Abd Allah informed us, saying: 'Ali informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-A'azz Abu Muslim, who said: I bear witness about Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id that they both testified that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No group sits remembering Allah, the Exalted, except that the angels surround them, mercy covers them, and He mentions them among those who are with Him." [157] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/49.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shaybah related to us, saying: al-Furbani related to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shanba related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, concerning ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾: "The remembrance of Allah of the servant during the prayer is greater than the prayer." Ibn 'Awn said: its meaning is: the prayer you are in, and Allah's remembrance of you in it, is greater than what the prayer has forbidden you from, of indecency and wrongdoing. Ibn 'Ata' said: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ than that you should remain in disobedience while in it.

﴿And Allah knows what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 29, verse 46–55:

وَلا تُجادِلُوا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book⁠﴾. Al-Jidal (argument): twisting the opponent away from his position by way of debate. Its root meaning is strong twisting, and from it the falcon is called ajdal, because of the strength of its body's twisting and the vigour of its build. It is also said: al-jidal derives from al-jadalah, which is the ground, and it means that each of the two disputants seeks to overpower his companion and throw him down onto the jadalah, which is the earth.

إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ ﴿except in a way that is best⁠﴾: more gentle and more kind. It means fine speech, invitation to God, and proof through the signs and arguments of God.

إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ ﴿except those of them who do wrong⁠﴾. Mujahid said: it means that if they say something evil, then you say something good. إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ, that is, those who refused to give the jizyah and took up war; those are the ones who were to be confronted and argued with by the sword, until they accept Islam or acknowledge the jizyah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are the people of war who have no covenant, so argue with them by the sword. Ibn Zayd said: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ refers to those who persist in their disbelief after the proof has been established against them.

The meaning of the verse: "except those who wronged you," because all of them are wrongdoers. Qatadah and Muqatil said: this verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God⁠﴾ [[Surah al-Tawbah: 29.]] ... the verse.

وَقُولُوا آمَنَّا بِالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنا وَأُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ ﴿And say: "We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you⁠﴾.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ibn Abi Namlah al-Ansari informed me that Abu Namlah told him, and his name was [Ammar] [[In Usd al-Ghabah (5/313): 'Ammar ibn Ma'an ibn Zurarah, and it is said: 'Umar.]]

That while he was sitting with the Messenger of God ﷺ, a man from the Jews came and passed by a funeral bier.

He said: "O Muhammad, can this bier speak?" The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "God knows best." The Jew said: "It does speak."

The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When the People of the Book narrate to you, do not confirm them and do not deny them, but say: 'We believe in God, His books and His messengers.' If it is false, you have not confirmed it; and if it is true, you have not denied it" [158] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/136.]].

Abu Salamah narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the people of Islam, so the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Do not confirm the People of the Book, nor deny them," and ﴿And say: "We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you"⁠﴾ ... the verse" [159] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 6/426.]].

Sufyan and Mas'ud narrated, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: While a man from the People of the Book was narrating to his companions, and they were glorifying God, whenever he mentioned something of their affairs, they came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said: "Do not confirm them, nor deny them, but say: 'We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you'" [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/147; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 21/6.]] [160].

وَإِلهُنا وَإِلهُكُمْ واحِدٌ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ ﴿Our God and your God is one, and to Him we are submitting⁠﴾. وَكَذلِكَ ﴿And thus⁠﴾: that is, just as We sent down the Book to them.

أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ ﴿We have sent down to you the Book⁠﴾. فَالَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ ﴿So those to whom We have given the Book believe in it⁠﴾: meaning the believers among the People of the Book, such as 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and his companions.

وَمِنْ هؤُلاءِ ﴿And among these⁠﴾ [[In the Isfahan manuscript: "And among these, i.e., the people of Makkah, there are those who believe in it, and they are the believers of the people of Makkah. Muhammad ibn Jarir said regarding (those to whom We have given the Book) that they are those from before you who believe in it, and among these ... etc."]] ﴿those who are among you today⁠﴾ believe in it. وَما يَجْحَدُ بِآياتِنا إِلَّا الْكافِرُونَ ﴿And none deny Our signs except the disbelievers⁠﴾. Qatadah said: denial only occurs after knowledge.

وَما كُنْتَ تَتْلُوا ﴿And you did not recite⁠﴾, O Muhammad, مِنْ قَبْلِهِ ﴿before it⁠﴾: that is, before this Book which We sent down to you, مِنْ كِتابٍ ﴿any book⁠﴾ وَلا تَخُطُّهُ ﴿nor did you write it⁠﴾, تكتبه ﴿with your right hand⁠﴾ بِيَمِينِكَ ﴿with your right hand⁠﴾ إِذاً لَارْتابَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ ﴿Otherwise, the falsifiers would have had doubt⁠﴾. It means: had you been writing or reading books before the revelation, the falsifiers, that is the polytheists of Makkah, would have doubted and said: "This is something Muhammad learned and wrote down." Qatadah said this.

Muqatil said: الْمُبْطِلُونَ are the Jews, and the meaning of the verse is: they would have doubted you and accused you, O Muhammad, and said: "The one whose description we find in the Torah is an unlettered person who neither reads nor writes."

بَلْ هُوَ ﴿Rather, it⁠﴾, meaning the Qur'an, آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ ﴿are clear signs⁠﴾, according to al-Hasan. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: بَلْ هُوَ, meaning Muhammad ﷺ, and the knowledge that he is unlettered, are clear signs فِي صُدُورِ [[In the Isfahan manuscript: "those given knowledge."]] أهل العلم from among the People of the Book [[In a second manuscript: "you find in your books."]] يجدونها in their books. The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn al-Sumayqa': بل هي آيات.

وَما يَجْحَدُ بِآياتِنا إِلَّا الظَّالِمُونَ ﴿And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers⁠﴾. وَقالُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آياتٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ ﴿And they say: "Why were not signs sent down to him from his Lord⁠﴾, as were sent down to the prophets before you?" Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Ayyub, and 'Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr read آية in the singular; the rest read آياتٌ in the plural, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it, because of His saying: ﴿Say: the signs are only with God; and when He wills, He sends them down⁠﴾, and I do not possess them, nor are they in my hand.

وَإِنَّما أَنَا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ ﴿I am only a clear warner⁠﴾. أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّا أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ يُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, which is recited to them?⁠﴾ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَرَحْمَةً وَذِكْرى لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ ﴿Indeed, in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe⁠﴾. This is the answer to their saying: لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آياتٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ.

Hajjaj narrated, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Yahya ibn Ja'dah, that some Muslims came to the Prophet of God (peace be upon him) with books they had written, containing some of what the Jews say. When he looked at them he threw them away and said: "Enough of folly for a people, or misguidance for a people, that they turn away from what their own prophet brought them to what was brought by someone other than their prophet, to a people other than them" [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 21/10.]] [161]. Then ﴿Is it not sufficient for them⁠﴾ ... the verse was revealed.

قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ شَهِيداً ﴿Say: "God is sufficient as a witness between me and you⁠﴾, that I am His messenger, and that this Qur'an is His Book. يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth⁠﴾. وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالْباطِلِ وَكَفَرُوا بِاللَّهِ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ ﴿And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in God—it is those who are the losers⁠﴾.

وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالْعَذابِ ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment⁠﴾. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith [[In the Isfahan manuscript: al-Harith.]] when he said: ﴿So rain down on us stones from the sky⁠﴾, and said: ﴿Hasten for us our portion⁠﴾ ...

وَلَوْلا أَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى ﴿And if not for a specified term⁠﴾ concerning the descent of the punishment. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means that I promised you I would not punish your people nor destroy them, and would delay their punishment until the Day of Resurrection. Its explanation is His saying: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time⁠﴾ [[Surah al-Qamar: 46.]] ... the verse. Al-Dahhak said: it means the duration of their lives in this world. It has also been said: it refers to the Day of Badr.

لَجاءَهُمُ الْعَذابُ ﴿the punishment would have come to them⁠﴾. وَلَيَأْتِيَنَّهُمْ ﴿and it will surely come to them⁠﴾, meaning the punishment; it has also been said the term is meant, بَغْتَةً ﴿suddenly⁠﴾ وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ ﴿while they do not perceive⁠﴾. يَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالْعَذابِ ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment⁠﴾. وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمُحِيطَةٌ بِالْكافِرِينَ ﴿And indeed, Hell is surrounding the disbelievers⁠﴾, so that none of them remains except that he enters it. It has also been said: this is connected to His saying: يَوْمَ يَغْشاهُمُ ﴿The Day it will cover them⁠﴾, that is, the punishment will reach them, مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ ﴿from above them and from beneath their feet⁠﴾. That is: when the punishment covers them, Hell surrounds them.

وَيَقُولُ ﴿And He will say⁠﴾ — with the letter ya' (يَقُولُ) read by al-Kufi, Nafi' and Ayyub; the others read it with nun (نَقُولُ) — ذُوقُوا ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ ﴿Taste what you used to do⁠﴾.

Sufyan and Mas'ud narrated, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: While a man from the People of the Book was narrating to his companions, and they were glorifying God, whenever he mentioned something of their affairs, they came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said: "Do not confirm them, nor deny them, but say: 'We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you'" [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/147; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 21/6.]] [160].

وَإِلهُنا وَإِلهُكُمْ واحِدٌ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ ﴿Our God and your God is one, and to Him we are submitting⁠﴾. وَكَذلِكَ ﴿And thus⁠﴾: that is, just as We sent down the Book to them.

أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ ﴿We have sent down to you the Book⁠﴾. فَالَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ ﴿So those to whom We have given the Book believe in it⁠﴾: meaning the believers among the People of the Book, such as 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and his companions.

وَمِنْ هؤُلاءِ ﴿And among these⁠﴾ [[In the Isfahan manuscript: "And among these, i.e., the people of Makkah, there are those who believe in it, and they are the believers of the people of Makkah. Muhammad ibn Jarir said regarding (those to whom We have given the Book) that they are those from before you who believe in it, and among these ... etc."]] ﴿those who are among you today⁠﴾ believe in it. وَما يَجْحَدُ بِآياتِنا إِلَّا الْكافِرُونَ ﴿And none deny Our signs except the disbelievers⁠﴾. Qatadah said: denial only occurs after knowledge.

وَما كُنْتَ تَتْلُوا ﴿And you did not recite⁠﴾, O Muhammad, مِنْ قَبْلِهِ ﴿before it⁠﴾: that is, before this Book which We sent down to you, مِنْ كِتابٍ ﴿any book⁠﴾ وَلا تَخُطُّهُ ﴿nor did you write it⁠﴾, تكتبه ﴿with your right hand⁠﴾ بِيَمِينِكَ ﴿with your right hand⁠﴾ إِذاً لَارْتابَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ ﴿Otherwise, the falsifiers would have had doubt⁠﴾. It means: had you been writing or reading books before the revelation, the falsifiers, that is the polytheists of Makkah, would have doubted and said: "This is something Muhammad learned and wrote down." Qatadah said this.

Muqatil said: الْمُبْطِلُونَ are the Jews, and the meaning of the verse is: they would have doubted you and accused you, O Muhammad, and said: "The one whose description we find in the Torah is an unlettered person who neither reads nor writes."

بَلْ هُوَ ﴿Rather, it⁠﴾, meaning the Qur'an, آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ ﴿are clear signs⁠﴾, according to al-Hasan. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: بَلْ هُوَ, meaning Muhammad ﷺ, and the knowledge that he is unlettered, are clear signs فِي صُدُورِ [[In the Isfahan manuscript: "those given knowledge."]] أهل العلم from among the People of the Book [[In a second manuscript: "you find in your books."]] يجدونها in their books. The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn al-Sumayqa': بل هي آيات.

وَما يَجْحَدُ بِآياتِنا إِلَّا الظَّالِمُونَ ﴿And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers⁠﴾. وَقالُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آياتٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ ﴿And they say: "Why were not signs sent down to him from his Lord⁠﴾, as were sent down to the prophets before you?" Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Ayyub, and 'Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr read آية in the singular; the rest read آياتٌ in the plural, and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it, because of His saying: ﴿Say: the signs are only with God; and when He wills, He sends them down⁠﴾, and I do not possess them, nor are they in my hand.

وَإِنَّما أَنَا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ ﴿I am only a clear warner⁠﴾. أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّا أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ يُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, which is recited to them?⁠﴾ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَرَحْمَةً وَذِكْرى لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ ﴿Indeed, in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe⁠﴾. This is the answer to their saying: لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آياتٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ.

Hajjaj narrated, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Yahya ibn Ja'dah, that some Muslims came to the Prophet of God (peace be upon him) with books they had written, containing some of what the Jews say. When he looked at them he threw them away and said: "Enough of folly for a people, or misguidance for a people, that they turn away from what their own prophet brought them to what was brought by someone other than their prophet, to a people other than them" [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 21/10.]] [161]. Then ﴿Is it not sufficient for them⁠﴾ ... the verse was revealed.

قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ شَهِيداً ﴿Say: "God is sufficient as a witness between me and you⁠﴾, that I am His messenger, and that this Qur'an is His Book. يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth⁠﴾. وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالْباطِلِ وَكَفَرُوا بِاللَّهِ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ ﴿And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in God—it is those who are the losers⁠﴾.

وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالْعَذابِ ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment⁠﴾. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith [[In the Isfahan manuscript: al-Harith.]] when he said: ﴿So rain down on us stones from the sky⁠﴾, and said: ﴿Hasten for us our portion⁠﴾ ...

وَلَوْلا أَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى ﴿And if not for a specified term⁠﴾ concerning the descent of the punishment. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means that I promised you I would not punish your people nor destroy them, and would delay their punishment until the Day of Resurrection. Its explanation is His saying: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time⁠﴾ [[Surah al-Qamar: 46.]] ... the verse. Al-Dahhak said: it means the duration of their lives in this world. It has also been said: it refers to the Day of Badr.

لَجاءَهُمُ الْعَذابُ ﴿the punishment would have come to them⁠﴾. وَلَيَأْتِيَنَّهُمْ ﴿and it will surely come to them⁠﴾, meaning the punishment; it has also been said the term is meant, بَغْتَةً ﴿suddenly⁠﴾ وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ ﴿while they do not perceive⁠﴾. يَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالْعَذابِ ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment⁠﴾. وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمُحِيطَةٌ بِالْكافِرِينَ ﴿And indeed, Hell is surrounding the disbelievers⁠﴾, so that none of them remains except that he enters it. It has also been said: this is connected to His saying: يَوْمَ يَغْشاهُمُ ﴿The Day it will cover them⁠﴾, that is, the punishment will reach them, مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ ﴿from above them and from beneath their feet⁠﴾. That is: when the punishment covers them, Hell surrounds them.

وَيَقُولُ ﴿And He will say⁠﴾ — with the letter ya' (يَقُولُ) read by al-Kufi, Nafi' and Ayyub; the others read it with nun (نَقُولُ) — ذُوقُوا ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ ﴿Taste what you used to do⁠﴾.

﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾

Read with the yā' (ي) of "ʿibādiya" pronounced with a sukūn (إرسال الياء) by Ḥafṣ... Hmm, let me state this plainly: the yā' is pronounced without a fatḥa (إرسال الياء) according to the reading of the Iraqis, other than ʿĀṣim; the rest read it with a fatḥa.

﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي﴾

The yā' is read with a fatḥa (مفتوحة الياء) by Ibn ʿĀmir; others read it with a sukūn (ساكنة). ﴿وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾

That is, worship Me alone, without obeying any creature in disobedience to Me. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If one acts with sin in a land, then flee [in another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: leave it], for ﴿My earth is spacious﴾." [In another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAṭāʾ said: "If you are commanded to sin, then flee from it, for My earth is spacious." See the Tafsir of al-Ṭabarī: 21/12.]

Mujāhid: ﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾ means: so emigrate and strive (فهاجروا وجاهدوا).

Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: it was revealed concerning the oppressed believers who were in Mecca and could not openly display their faith or worship the Most Merciful. He urges them to emigrate and says to them: "Indeed the land of Medina is spacious and secure." Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: ﴿My earth is spacious﴾ means: My provision for you is abundant; I bring forth from the earth what is in it.

We were informed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid [in the Isfahan copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-Wazzān], who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Shādhān informed us, who said: Jīghwayh ibn Muḥammad al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr al-Nājī, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise and will be the companion of Abraham and Muhammad (peace be upon them both)." [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 5/347.] [162]

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ Therefore, do not dwell in the abode of the polytheists.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — "ghurafan" means lofty chambers (عَلالي). Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read the verb with a tāʾ (بالتاء); others read it with a yāʾ (بالياء), meaning: "He will surely settle them [in them]." ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin" means "and how many" (وكم). That is because of:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca, who had been harmed by the polytheists: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live as neighbors of the wrongdoers there." [163] [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/360.]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we leave for Medina when we have there no house, no property, and no wealth? Who will feed us there and give us drink?" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — that is, many a creature that has need of food does not carry its provision, and Allah provides for it, meaning the birds and the beasts.

﴿اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ day by day. ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, and you feared that separation from our homeland would bring poverty. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is in your hearts and of where your affairs will end.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqāq narrated to us, and he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zurāra al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl al-Jawzī [in the Isfahan copy: al-Jazarī] narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began picking dates with his hand and eating. He said: "Eat, O Ibn ʿUmar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food nor found any."

I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, if you asked your Lord, He would give me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satisfied one day. How will it be with you, O Ibn ʿUmar, when you grow old and remain among the rabble of people who hoard a year's provision and whose certainty weakens?" [Al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/149; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/359; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 3/430; and with variation in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/321.] [164] Then ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)… the verse.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Ibn Ḥunaysh narrated to us: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAlī ibn al-Arqam [in the Isfahan copy: al-Aqmar], concerning ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾, he said: "It does not store anything for tomorrow."

Sufyān said: "Nothing that Allah has created stores up except the human being, the mouse, and the ant."

﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ. اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهَا لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ. وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ﴾ — meaning the enduring, everlasting one, which has no cessation and no death in it. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — but they do not know this.

﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ وَخَافُوا الْغَرَقَ وَالْهَلَاكَ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ. لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ — that they may deny Our favour in saving them, and the rest of the verse: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — the lām here is read with a jazm (جزم لامه) by al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf and Ayyūb; it is read variously from ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr; the rest read it with a kasra (بكسر اللام), and Abū ʿUbayd chose this, because the speech is in sequence (لكون الكلام نسقا). Whoever reads with a jazm argues from the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "yumtiʿū." ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid — concerning what he permitted me to narrate from him — who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Askat narrated to us, who said: ʿAqqāl narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Salmān narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Dīnār narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliya recite "li-yakfurū bimā ātaynāhum fa-tamattaʿū fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn" with a yāʾ. The kasra (on the lām, as in liyakfurū) is for "kay" (so that), and the jazm is for threat (التهديد).

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَمًا آمِنًا وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ أَفَبِالْبَاطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — by idols — ﴿وَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ — meaning faith. ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ — they claimed that Allah has a partner, and they said when they committed an indecency: ﴿وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَا آبَاءَنَا وَاللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا﴾ [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 28.]

﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — Muhammad and the Qur'an — ﴿لَمَّا جَاءَهُ﴾ — ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْكَافِرِينَ. وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾ — that is, those who fought for Our sake against Our enemies, for the victory of Our religion, that We may make them steadfast in what they fought for.

Abū Sūra said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in the raid (الغزو) ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سَبِيلَ الشَّهَادَةِ أَوِ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ — the path of martyrdom or forgiveness.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, who said: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna say: "When people differ, look at what the people of the frontier (ahl al-thaghr) hold to, for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾."

al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in seeking knowledge ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْعَمَلِ بِهِ﴾ — the paths of acting upon it.

Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Aḥmad informed me, who said: Abū al-Ṭayyib Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdūn narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Jawārī narrated to us, who said: Abū Aḥmad — meaning ʿAbbās al-Hamdānī — and Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾: "Those who act upon what they know, their Lord guides them to what they do not know."

It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he spoke some words while a group of scholars was present, and al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ said to him: "By what were you given this knowledge, O Abū Marwān?" He said: "Woe to you, O Waḍīn! Our knowledge of what we did not know falls short only because of our shortcoming in acting upon what we know. If we had acted upon some of what we know, it would have bequeathed to us knowledge that our bodies could not bear."

It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "Wisdom says: whoever seeks me and does not find me, let him seek me in two places: that he act upon the best of what he knows, or that he abandon the worst of what he knows."

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي طَاعَتِنَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ ثَوَابِنَا﴾ — the paths of Our reward. Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by emigration ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الثَّبَاتِ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ﴾ — the paths of steadfastness in faith. It was also said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by steadfastness in faith ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ دُخُولِ الْجِنَانِ﴾ — the paths of entering the gardens of Paradise. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي إِقَامَةِ السُّنَّةِ لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — the paths to Paradise. Then he said: "The likeness of the Sunna in this world is like the likeness of Paradise in the hereafter. Whoever enters Paradise in the hereafter is safe; likewise whoever adheres to the Sunna in this world is safe." al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "In it there is inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr); its meaning is: those whom We guided to Our path strove for Us."

﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — with victory and help in their worldly life, and with reward and forgiveness in their final abode.

﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾

Read with the yā' (ي) of "ʿibādiya" pronounced with a sukūn (إرسال الياء) by Ḥafṣ... Hmm, let me state this plainly: the yā' is pronounced without a fatḥa (إرسال الياء) according to the reading of the Iraqis, other than ʿĀṣim; the rest read it with a fatḥa.

﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي﴾

The yā' is read with a fatḥa (مفتوحة الياء) by Ibn ʿĀmir; others read it with a sukūn (ساكنة). ﴿وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾

That is, worship Me alone, without obeying any creature in disobedience to Me. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If one acts with sin in a land, then flee [in another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: leave it], for ﴿My earth is spacious﴾." [In another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAṭāʾ said: "If you are commanded to sin, then flee from it, for My earth is spacious." See the Tafsir of al-Ṭabarī: 21/12.]

Mujāhid: ﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾ means: so emigrate and strive (فهاجروا وجاهدوا).

Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: it was revealed concerning the oppressed believers who were in Mecca and could not openly display their faith or worship the Most Merciful. He urges them to emigrate and says to them: "Indeed the land of Medina is spacious and secure." Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: ﴿My earth is spacious﴾ means: My provision for you is abundant; I bring forth from the earth what is in it.

We were informed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid [in the Isfahan copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-Wazzān], who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Shādhān informed us, who said: Jīghwayh ibn Muḥammad al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr al-Nājī, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise and will be the companion of Abraham and Muhammad (peace be upon them both)." [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 5/347.] [162]

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ Therefore, do not dwell in the abode of the polytheists.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — "ghurafan" means lofty chambers (عَلالي). Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read the verb with a tāʾ (بالتاء); others read it with a yāʾ (بالياء), meaning: "He will surely settle them [in them]." ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin" means "and how many" (وكم). That is because of:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca, who had been harmed by the polytheists: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live as neighbors of the wrongdoers there." [163] [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/360.]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we leave for Medina when we have there no house, no property, and no wealth? Who will feed us there and give us drink?" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — that is, many a creature that has need of food does not carry its provision, and Allah provides for it, meaning the birds and the beasts.

﴿اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ day by day. ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, and you feared that separation from our homeland would bring poverty. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is in your hearts and of where your affairs will end.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqāq narrated to us, and he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zurāra al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl al-Jawzī [in the Isfahan copy: al-Jazarī] narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began picking dates with his hand and eating. He said: "Eat, O Ibn ʿUmar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food nor found any."

I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, if you asked your Lord, He would give me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satisfied one day. How will it be with you, O Ibn ʿUmar, when you grow old and remain among the rabble of people who hoard a year's provision and whose certainty weakens?" [Al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/149; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/359; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 3/430; and with variation in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/321.] [164] Then ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)… the verse.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Ibn Ḥunaysh narrated to us: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAlī ibn al-Arqam [in the Isfahan copy: al-Aqmar], concerning ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾, he said: "It does not store anything for tomorrow."

Sufyān said: "Nothing that Allah has created stores up except the human being, the mouse, and the ant."

﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ. اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهَا لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ. وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ﴾ — meaning the enduring, everlasting one, which has no cessation and no death in it. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — but they do not know this.

﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ وَخَافُوا الْغَرَقَ وَالْهَلَاكَ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ. لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ — that they may deny Our favour in saving them, and the rest of the verse: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — the lām here is read with a jazm (جزم لامه) by al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf and Ayyūb; it is read variously from ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr; the rest read it with a kasra (بكسر اللام), and Abū ʿUbayd chose this, because the speech is in sequence (لكون الكلام نسقا). Whoever reads with a jazm argues from the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "yumtiʿū." ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid — concerning what he permitted me to narrate from him — who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Askat narrated to us, who said: ʿAqqāl narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Salmān narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Dīnār narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliya recite "li-yakfurū bimā ātaynāhum fa-tamattaʿū fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn" with a yāʾ. The kasra (on the lām, as in liyakfurū) is for "kay" (so that), and the jazm is for threat (التهديد).

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَمًا آمِنًا وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ أَفَبِالْبَاطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — by idols — ﴿وَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ — meaning faith. ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ — they claimed that Allah has a partner, and they said when they committed an indecency: ﴿وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَا آبَاءَنَا وَاللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا﴾ [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 28.]

﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — Muhammad and the Qur'an — ﴿لَمَّا جَاءَهُ﴾ — ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْكَافِرِينَ. وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾ — that is, those who fought for Our sake against Our enemies, for the victory of Our religion, that We may make them steadfast in what they fought for.

Abū Sūra said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in the raid (الغزو) ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سَبِيلَ الشَّهَادَةِ أَوِ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ — the path of martyrdom or forgiveness.

Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read the verb with a tāʾ (بالتاء); others read it with a yāʾ (بالياء), meaning: "He will surely settle them [in them]." ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin" means "and how many" (وكم). That is because of:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca, who had been harmed by the polytheists: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live as neighbors of the wrongdoers there." [163] [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/360.]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we leave for Medina when we have there no house, no property, and no wealth? Who will feed us there and give us drink?" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — that is, many a creature that has need of food does not carry its provision, and Allah provides for it, meaning the birds and the beasts.

﴿اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ day by day. ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, and you feared that separation from our homeland would bring poverty. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is in your hearts and of where your affairs will end.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqāq narrated to us, and he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zurāra al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl al-Jawzī [in the Isfahan copy: al-Jazarī] narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began picking dates with his hand and eating. He said: "Eat, O Ibn ʿUmar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food nor found any."

I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, if you asked your Lord, He would give me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satisfied one day. How will it be with you, O Ibn ʿUmar, when you grow old and remain among the rabble of people who hoard a year's provision and whose certainty weakens?" [Al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/149; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/359; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 3/430; and with variation in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/321.] [164] Then ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)… the verse.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Ibn Ḥunaysh narrated to us: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAlī ibn al-Arqam [in the Isfahan copy: al-Aqmar], concerning ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾, he said: "It does not store anything for tomorrow."

Sufyān said: "Nothing that Allah has created stores up except the human being, the mouse, and the ant."

﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ. اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهَا لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ. وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ﴾ — meaning the enduring, everlasting one, which has no cessation and no death in it. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — but they do not know this.

﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ وَخَافُوا الْغَرَقَ وَالْهَلَاكَ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ. لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ — that they may deny Our favour in saving them, and the rest of the verse: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — the lām here is read with a jazm (جزم لامه) by al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf and Ayyūb; it is read variously from ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr; the rest read it with a kasra (بكسر اللام), and Abū ʿUbayd chose this, because the speech is in sequence (لكون الكلام نسقا). Whoever reads with a jazm argues from the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "yumtiʿū." ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid — concerning what he permitted me to narrate from him — who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Askat narrated to us, who said: ʿAqqāl narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Salmān narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Dīnār narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliya recite "li-yakfurū bimā ātaynāhum fa-tamattaʿū fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn" with a yāʾ. The kasra (on the lām, as in liyakfurū) is for "kay" (so that), and the jazm is for threat (التهديد).

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَمًا آمِنًا وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ أَفَبِالْبَاطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — by idols — ﴿وَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ — meaning faith. ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ — they claimed that Allah has a partner, and they said when they committed an indecency: ﴿وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَا آبَاءَنَا وَاللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا﴾ [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 28.]

﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — Muhammad and the Qur'an — ﴿لَمَّا جَاءَهُ﴾ — ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْكَافِرِينَ. وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾ — that is, those who fought for Our sake against Our enemies, for the victory of Our religion, that We may make them steadfast in what they fought for.

Abū Sūra said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in the raid (الغزو) ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سَبِيلَ الشَّهَادَةِ أَوِ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ — the path of martyrdom or forgiveness.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, who said: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna say: "When people differ, look at what the people of the frontier (ahl al-thaghr) hold to, for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾."

al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in seeking knowledge ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْعَمَلِ بِهِ﴾ — the paths of acting upon it.

Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Aḥmad informed me, who said: Abū al-Ṭayyib Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdūn narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Jawārī narrated to us, who said: Abū Aḥmad — meaning ʿAbbās al-Hamdānī — and Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾: "Those who act upon what they know, their Lord guides them to what they do not know."

It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he spoke some words while a group of scholars was present, and al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ said to him: "By what were you given this knowledge, O Abū Marwān?" He said: "Woe to you, O Waḍīn! Our knowledge of what we did not know falls short only because of our shortcoming in acting upon what we know. If we had acted upon some of what we know, it would have bequeathed to us knowledge that our bodies could not bear."

It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "Wisdom says: whoever seeks me and does not find me, let him seek me in two places: that he act upon the best of what he knows, or that he abandon the worst of what he knows."

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي طَاعَتِنَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ ثَوَابِنَا﴾ — the paths of Our reward. Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by emigration ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الثَّبَاتِ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ﴾ — the paths of steadfastness in faith. It was also said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by steadfastness in faith ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ دُخُولِ الْجِنَانِ﴾ — the paths of entering the gardens of Paradise. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي إِقَامَةِ السُّنَّةِ لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — the paths to Paradise. Then he said: "The likeness of the Sunna in this world is like the likeness of Paradise in the hereafter. Whoever enters Paradise in the hereafter is safe; likewise whoever adheres to the Sunna in this world is safe." al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "In it there is inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr); its meaning is: those whom We guided to Our path strove for Us."

﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — with victory and help in their worldly life, and with reward and forgiveness in their final abode.

﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾

Read with the yā' (ي) of "ʿibādiya" pronounced with a sukūn (إرسال الياء) by Ḥafṣ... Hmm, let me state this plainly: the yā' is pronounced without a fatḥa (إرسال الياء) according to the reading of the Iraqis, other than ʿĀṣim; the rest read it with a fatḥa.

﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي﴾

The yā' is read with a fatḥa (مفتوحة الياء) by Ibn ʿĀmir; others read it with a sukūn (ساكنة). ﴿وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾

That is, worship Me alone, without obeying any creature in disobedience to Me. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If one acts with sin in a land, then flee [in another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: leave it], for ﴿My earth is spacious﴾." [In another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAṭāʾ said: "If you are commanded to sin, then flee from it, for My earth is spacious." See the Tafsir of al-Ṭabarī: 21/12.]

Mujāhid: ﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾ means: so emigrate and strive (فهاجروا وجاهدوا).

Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: it was revealed concerning the oppressed believers who were in Mecca and could not openly display their faith or worship the Most Merciful. He urges them to emigrate and says to them: "Indeed the land of Medina is spacious and secure." Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: ﴿My earth is spacious﴾ means: My provision for you is abundant; I bring forth from the earth what is in it.

We were informed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid [in the Isfahan copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-Wazzān], who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Shādhān informed us, who said: Jīghwayh ibn Muḥammad al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr al-Nājī, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise and will be the companion of Abraham and Muhammad (peace be upon them both)." [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 5/347.] [162]

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Ibn Ḥunaysh narrated to us: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAlī ibn al-Arqam [in the Isfahan copy: al-Aqmar], concerning ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾, he said: "It does not store anything for tomorrow."

Sufyān said: "Nothing that Allah has created stores up except the human being, the mouse, and the ant."

﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ. اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهَا لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ. وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ﴾ — meaning the enduring, everlasting one, which has no cessation and no death in it. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — but they do not know this.

﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ وَخَافُوا الْغَرَقَ وَالْهَلَاكَ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ. لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ — that they may deny Our favour in saving them, and the rest of the verse: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — the lām here is read with a jazm (جزم لامه) by al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf and Ayyūb; it is read variously from ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr; the rest read it with a kasra (بكسر اللام), and Abū ʿUbayd chose this, because the speech is in sequence (لكون الكلام نسقا). Whoever reads with a jazm argues from the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "yumtiʿū." ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid — concerning what he permitted me to narrate from him — who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Askat narrated to us, who said: ʿAqqāl narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Salmān narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Dīnār narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliya recite "li-yakfurū bimā ātaynāhum fa-tamattaʿū fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn" with a yāʾ. The kasra (on the lām, as in liyakfurū) is for "kay" (so that), and the jazm is for threat (التهديد).

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَمًا آمِنًا وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ أَفَبِالْبَاطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — by idols — ﴿وَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ — meaning faith. ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ — they claimed that Allah has a partner, and they said when they committed an indecency: ﴿وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَا آبَاءَنَا وَاللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا﴾ [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 28.]

﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — Muhammad and the Qur'an — ﴿لَمَّا جَاءَهُ﴾ — ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْكَافِرِينَ. وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾ — that is, those who fought for Our sake against Our enemies, for the victory of Our religion, that We may make them steadfast in what they fought for.

Abū Sūra said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in the raid (الغزو) ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سَبِيلَ الشَّهَادَةِ أَوِ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ — the path of martyrdom or forgiveness.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, who said: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna say: "When people differ, look at what the people of the frontier (ahl al-thaghr) hold to, for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾."

al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in seeking knowledge ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْعَمَلِ بِهِ﴾ — the paths of acting upon it.

Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Aḥmad informed me, who said: Abū al-Ṭayyib Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdūn narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Jawārī narrated to us, who said: Abū Aḥmad — meaning ʿAbbās al-Hamdānī — and Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾: "Those who act upon what they know, their Lord guides them to what they do not know."

It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he spoke some words while a group of scholars was present, and al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ said to him: "By what were you given this knowledge, O Abū Marwān?" He said: "Woe to you, O Waḍīn! Our knowledge of what we did not know falls short only because of our shortcoming in acting upon what we know. If we had acted upon some of what we know, it would have bequeathed to us knowledge that our bodies could not bear."

It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "Wisdom says: whoever seeks me and does not find me, let him seek me in two places: that he act upon the best of what he knows, or that he abandon the worst of what he knows."

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي طَاعَتِنَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ ثَوَابِنَا﴾ — the paths of Our reward. Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by emigration ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الثَّبَاتِ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ﴾ — the paths of steadfastness in faith. It was also said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by steadfastness in faith ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ دُخُولِ الْجِنَانِ﴾ — the paths of entering the gardens of Paradise. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي إِقَامَةِ السُّنَّةِ لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — the paths to Paradise. Then he said: "The likeness of the Sunna in this world is like the likeness of Paradise in the hereafter. Whoever enters Paradise in the hereafter is safe; likewise whoever adheres to the Sunna in this world is safe." al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "In it there is inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr); its meaning is: those whom We guided to Our path strove for Us."

﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — with victory and help in their worldly life, and with reward and forgiveness in their final abode.

﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾

Read with the yā' (ي) of "ʿibādiya" pronounced with a sukūn (إرسال الياء) by Ḥafṣ... Hmm, let me state this plainly: the yā' is pronounced without a fatḥa (إرسال الياء) according to the reading of the Iraqis, other than ʿĀṣim; the rest read it with a fatḥa.

﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي﴾

The yā' is read with a fatḥa (مفتوحة الياء) by Ibn ʿĀmir; others read it with a sukūn (ساكنة). ﴿وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾

That is, worship Me alone, without obeying any creature in disobedience to Me. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If one acts with sin in a land, then flee [in another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: leave it], for ﴿My earth is spacious﴾." [In another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAṭāʾ said: "If you are commanded to sin, then flee from it, for My earth is spacious." See the Tafsir of al-Ṭabarī: 21/12.]

Mujāhid: ﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾ means: so emigrate and strive (فهاجروا وجاهدوا).

Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: it was revealed concerning the oppressed believers who were in Mecca and could not openly display their faith or worship the Most Merciful. He urges them to emigrate and says to them: "Indeed the land of Medina is spacious and secure." Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: ﴿My earth is spacious﴾ means: My provision for you is abundant; I bring forth from the earth what is in it.

We were informed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid [in the Isfahan copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-Wazzān], who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Shādhān informed us, who said: Jīghwayh ibn Muḥammad al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr al-Nājī, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise and will be the companion of Abraham and Muhammad (peace be upon them both)." [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 5/347.] [162]

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ Therefore, do not dwell in the abode of the polytheists.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — "ghurafan" means lofty chambers (عَلالي). Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read the verb with a tāʾ (بالتاء); others read it with a yāʾ (بالياء), meaning: "He will surely settle them [in them]." ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin" means "and how many" (وكم). That is because of:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca, who had been harmed by the polytheists: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live as neighbors of the wrongdoers there." [163] [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/360.]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we leave for Medina when we have there no house, no property, and no wealth? Who will feed us there and give us drink?" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — that is, many a creature that has need of food does not carry its provision, and Allah provides for it, meaning the birds and the beasts.

﴿اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ day by day. ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, and you feared that separation from our homeland would bring poverty. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is in your hearts and of where your affairs will end.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqāq narrated to us, and he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zurāra al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl al-Jawzī [in the Isfahan copy: al-Jazarī] narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began picking dates with his hand and eating. He said: "Eat, O Ibn ʿUmar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food nor found any."

I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, if you asked your Lord, He would give me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satisfied one day. How will it be with you, O Ibn ʿUmar, when you grow old and remain among the rabble of people who hoard a year's provision and whose certainty weakens?" [Al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/149; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/359; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 3/430; and with variation in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/321.] [164] Then ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)… the verse.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, who said: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna say: "When people differ, look at what the people of the frontier (ahl al-thaghr) hold to, for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾."

al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in seeking knowledge ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْعَمَلِ بِهِ﴾ — the paths of acting upon it.

Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Aḥmad informed me, who said: Abū al-Ṭayyib Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdūn narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Jawārī narrated to us, who said: Abū Aḥmad — meaning ʿAbbās al-Hamdānī — and Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾: "Those who act upon what they know, their Lord guides them to what they do not know."

It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he spoke some words while a group of scholars was present, and al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ said to him: "By what were you given this knowledge, O Abū Marwān?" He said: "Woe to you, O Waḍīn! Our knowledge of what we did not know falls short only because of our shortcoming in acting upon what we know. If we had acted upon some of what we know, it would have bequeathed to us knowledge that our bodies could not bear."

It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "Wisdom says: whoever seeks me and does not find me, let him seek me in two places: that he act upon the best of what he knows, or that he abandon the worst of what he knows."

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي طَاعَتِنَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ ثَوَابِنَا﴾ — the paths of Our reward. Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by emigration ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الثَّبَاتِ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ﴾ — the paths of steadfastness in faith. It was also said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by steadfastness in faith ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ دُخُولِ الْجِنَانِ﴾ — the paths of entering the gardens of Paradise. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي إِقَامَةِ السُّنَّةِ لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — the paths to Paradise. Then he said: "The likeness of the Sunna in this world is like the likeness of Paradise in the hereafter. Whoever enters Paradise in the hereafter is safe; likewise whoever adheres to the Sunna in this world is safe." al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "In it there is inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr); its meaning is: those whom We guided to Our path strove for Us."

﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — with victory and help in their worldly life, and with reward and forgiveness in their final abode.

﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾

Read with the yā' (ي) of "ʿibādiya" pronounced with a sukūn (إرسال الياء) by Ḥafṣ... Hmm, let me state this plainly: the yā' is pronounced without a fatḥa (إرسال الياء) according to the reading of the Iraqis, other than ʿĀṣim; the rest read it with a fatḥa.

﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي﴾

The yā' is read with a fatḥa (مفتوحة الياء) by Ibn ʿĀmir; others read it with a sukūn (ساكنة). ﴿وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾

That is, worship Me alone, without obeying any creature in disobedience to Me. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If one acts with sin in a land, then flee [in another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: leave it], for ﴿My earth is spacious﴾." [In another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAṭāʾ said: "If you are commanded to sin, then flee from it, for My earth is spacious." See the Tafsir of al-Ṭabarī: 21/12.]

Mujāhid: ﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾ means: so emigrate and strive (فهاجروا وجاهدوا).

Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: it was revealed concerning the oppressed believers who were in Mecca and could not openly display their faith or worship the Most Merciful. He urges them to emigrate and says to them: "Indeed the land of Medina is spacious and secure." Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: ﴿My earth is spacious﴾ means: My provision for you is abundant; I bring forth from the earth what is in it.

We were informed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid [in the Isfahan copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-Wazzān], who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Shādhān informed us, who said: Jīghwayh ibn Muḥammad al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr al-Nājī, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise and will be the companion of Abraham and Muhammad (peace be upon them both)." [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 5/347.] [162]

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ Therefore, do not dwell in the abode of the polytheists.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — "ghurafan" means lofty chambers (عَلالي). Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read the verb with a tāʾ (بالتاء); others read it with a yāʾ (بالياء), meaning: "He will surely settle them [in them]." ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin" means "and how many" (وكم). That is because of:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca, who had been harmed by the polytheists: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live as neighbors of the wrongdoers there." [163] [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/360.]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we leave for Medina when we have there no house, no property, and no wealth? Who will feed us there and give us drink?" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — that is, many a creature that has need of food does not carry its provision, and Allah provides for it, meaning the birds and the beasts.

﴿اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ day by day. ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, and you feared that separation from our homeland would bring poverty. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is in your hearts and of where your affairs will end.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqāq narrated to us, and he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zurāra al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl al-Jawzī [in the Isfahan copy: al-Jazarī] narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began picking dates with his hand and eating. He said: "Eat, O Ibn ʿUmar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food nor found any."

I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, if you asked your Lord, He would give me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satisfied one day. How will it be with you, O Ibn ʿUmar, when you grow old and remain among the rabble of people who hoard a year's provision and whose certainty weakens?" [Al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/149; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/359; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 3/430; and with variation in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/321.] [164] Then ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)… the verse.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Ibn Ḥunaysh narrated to us: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAlī ibn al-Arqam [in the Isfahan copy: al-Aqmar], concerning ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾, he said: "It does not store anything for tomorrow."

Sufyān said: "Nothing that Allah has created stores up except the human being, the mouse, and the ant."

﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ. اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهَا لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ. وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ﴾ — meaning the enduring, everlasting one, which has no cessation and no death in it. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — but they do not know this.

﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ وَخَافُوا الْغَرَقَ وَالْهَلَاكَ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ. لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ — that they may deny Our favour in saving them, and the rest of the verse: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — the lām here is read with a jazm (جزم لامه) by al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf and Ayyūb; it is read variously from ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr; the rest read it with a kasra (بكسر اللام), and Abū ʿUbayd chose this, because the speech is in sequence (لكون الكلام نسقا). Whoever reads with a jazm argues from the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "yumtiʿū." ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid — concerning what he permitted me to narrate from him — who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Askat narrated to us, who said: ʿAqqāl narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Salmān narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Dīnār narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliya recite "li-yakfurū bimā ātaynāhum fa-tamattaʿū fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn" with a yāʾ. Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: ﴿My earth is spacious﴾ means: My provision for you is abundant; I bring forth from the earth what is in it.

We were informed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid [in the Isfahan copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-Wazzān], who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Shādhān informed us, who said: Jīghwayh ibn Muḥammad al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr al-Nājī, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise and will be the companion of Abraham and Muhammad (peace be upon them both)." [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 5/347.] [162]

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ Therefore, do not dwell in the abode of the polytheists.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — "ghurafan" means lofty chambers (عَلالي). Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read the verb with a tāʾ (بالتاء); others read it with a yāʾ (بالياء), meaning: "He will surely settle them [in them]." ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin" means "and how many" (وكم). That is because of:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca, who had been harmed by the polytheists: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live as neighbors of the wrongdoers there." [163] [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/360.]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we leave for Medina when we have there no house, no property, and no wealth? Who will feed us there and give us drink?" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — that is, many a creature that has need of food does not carry its provision, and Allah provides for it, meaning the birds and the beasts.

﴿اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ day by day. ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, and you feared that separation from our homeland would bring poverty. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is in your hearts and of where your affairs will end.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqāq narrated to us, and he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zurāra al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl al-Jawzī [in the Isfahan copy: al-Jazarī] narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began picking dates with his hand and eating. He said: "Eat, O Ibn ʿUmar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food nor found any."

I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, if you asked your Lord, He would give me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satisfied one day. How will it be with you, O Ibn ʿUmar, when you grow old and remain among the rabble of people who hoard a year's provision and whose certainty weakens?" [Al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/149; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/359; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 3/430; and with variation in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/321.] [164] Then ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)… the verse.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Ibn Ḥunaysh narrated to us: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAlī ibn al-Arqam [in the Isfahan copy: al-Aqmar], concerning ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾, he said: "It does not store anything for tomorrow."

Sufyān said: "Nothing that Allah has created stores up except the human being, the mouse, and the ant."

﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ. اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهَا لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ. وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ﴾ — meaning the enduring, everlasting one, which has no cessation and no death in it. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — but they do not know this.

﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ وَخَافُوا الْغَرَقَ وَالْهَلَاكَ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ. لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ — that they may deny Our favour in saving them, and the rest of the verse: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — the lām here is read with a jazm (جزم لامه) by al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf and Ayyūb; it is read variously from ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr; the rest read it with a kasra (بكسر اللام), and Abū ʿUbayd chose this, because the speech is in sequence (لكون الكلام نسقا). Whoever reads with a jazm argues from the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "yumtiʿū." ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid — concerning what he permitted me to narrate from him — who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Askat narrated to us, who said: ʿAqqāl narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Salmān narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Dīnār narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliya recite "li-yakfurū bimā ātaynāhum fa-tamattaʿū fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn" with a yāʾ. The kasra (on the lām, as in liyakfurū) is for "kay" (so that), and the jazm is for threat (التهديد).

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَمًا آمِنًا وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ أَفَبِالْبَاطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — by idols — ﴿وَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ — meaning faith. ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ — they claimed that Allah has a partner, and they said when they committed an indecency: ﴿وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَا آبَاءَنَا وَاللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا﴾ [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 28.]

﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — Muhammad and the Qur'an — ﴿لَمَّا جَاءَهُ﴾ — ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْكَافِرِينَ. وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾ — that is, those who fought for Our sake against Our enemies, for the victory of Our religion, that We may make them steadfast in what they fought for.

Abū Sūra said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in the raid (الغزو) ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سَبِيلَ الشَّهَادَةِ أَوِ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ — the path of martyrdom or forgiveness.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, who said: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna say: "When people differ, look at what the people of the frontier (ahl al-thaghr) hold to, for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾."

al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in seeking knowledge ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْعَمَلِ بِهِ﴾ — the paths of acting upon it.

Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Aḥmad informed me, who said: Abū al-Ṭayyib Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdūn narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Jawārī narrated to us, who said: Abū Aḥmad — meaning ʿAbbās al-Hamdānī — and Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾: "Those who act upon what they know, their Lord guides them to what they do not know."

It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he spoke some words while a group of scholars was present, and al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ said to him: "By what were you given this knowledge, O Abū Marwān?" He said: "Woe to you, O Waḍīn! Our knowledge of what we did not know falls short only because of our shortcoming in acting upon what we know. If we had acted upon some of what we know, it would have bequeathed to us knowledge that our bodies could not bear."

It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "Wisdom says: whoever seeks me and does not find me, let him seek me in two places: that he act upon the best of what he knows, or that he abandon the worst of what he knows."

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي طَاعَتِنَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ ثَوَابِنَا﴾ — the paths of Our reward. Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by emigration ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الثَّبَاتِ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ﴾ — the paths of steadfastness in faith. It was also said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by steadfastness in faith ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ دُخُولِ الْجِنَانِ﴾ — the paths of entering the gardens of Paradise. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي إِقَامَةِ السُّنَّةِ لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — the paths to Paradise. Then he said: "The likeness of the Sunna in this world is like the likeness of Paradise in the hereafter. Whoever enters Paradise in the hereafter is safe; likewise whoever adheres to the Sunna in this world is safe." al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "In it there is inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr); its meaning is: those whom We guided to Our path strove for Us."

﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — with victory and help in their worldly life, and with reward and forgiveness in their final abode.

﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾
