Sufyān said: "Nothing that Allah has created stores up except the human being, the mouse, and the ant."

﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ. اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهَا لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ. وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ﴾ — meaning the enduring, everlasting one, which has no cessation and no death in it. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — but they do not know this.

﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ وَخَافُوا الْغَرَقَ وَالْهَلَاكَ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ. لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ — that they may deny Our favour in saving them, and the rest of the verse: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — the lām here is read with a jazm (جزم لامه) by al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf and Ayyūb; it is read variously from ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr; the rest read it with a kasra (بكسر اللام), and Abū ʿUbayd chose this, because the speech is in sequence (لكون الكلام نسقا). Whoever reads with a jazm argues from the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "yumtiʿū." ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid — concerning what he permitted me to narrate from him — who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Askat narrated to us, who said: ʿAqqāl narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Salmān narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Dīnār narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliya recite "li-yakfurū bimā ātaynāhum fa-tamattaʿū fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn" with a yāʾ. The kasra (on the lām, as in liyakfurū) is for "kay" (so that), and the jazm is for threat (التهديد).

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَمًا آمِنًا وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ أَفَبِالْبَاطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — by idols — ﴿وَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ — meaning faith. ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ — they claimed that Allah has a partner, and they said when they committed an indecency: ﴿وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَا آبَاءَنَا وَاللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا﴾ [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 28.]

﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — Muhammad and the Qur'an — ﴿لَمَّا جَاءَهُ﴾ — ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْكَافِرِينَ. وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾ — that is, those who fought for Our sake against Our enemies, for the victory of Our religion, that We may make them steadfast in what they fought for.

Abū Sūra said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in the raid (الغزو) ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سَبِيلَ الشَّهَادَةِ أَوِ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ — the path of martyrdom or forgiveness.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, who said: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna say: "When people differ, look at what the people of the frontier (ahl al-thaghr) hold to, for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾."

al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in seeking knowledge ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْعَمَلِ بِهِ﴾ — the paths of acting upon it.

Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Aḥmad informed me, who said: Abū al-Ṭayyib Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdūn narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Jawārī narrated to us, who said: Abū Aḥmad — meaning ʿAbbās al-Hamdānī — and Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾: "Those who act upon what they know, their Lord guides them to what they do not know."

It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he spoke some words while a group of scholars was present, and al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ said to him: "By what were you given this knowledge, O Abū Marwān?" He said: "Woe to you, O Waḍīn! Our knowledge of what we did not know falls short only because of our shortcoming in acting upon what we know. If we had acted upon some of what we know, it would have bequeathed to us knowledge that our bodies could not bear."

It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "Wisdom says: whoever seeks me and does not find me, let him seek me in two places: that he act upon the best of what he knows, or that he abandon the worst of what he knows."

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي طَاعَتِنَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ ثَوَابِنَا﴾ — the paths of Our reward. Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by emigration ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الثَّبَاتِ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ﴾ — the paths of steadfastness in faith. It was also said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by steadfastness in faith ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ دُخُولِ الْجِنَانِ﴾ — the paths of entering the gardens of Paradise. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي إِقَامَةِ السُّنَّةِ لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — the paths to Paradise. Then he said: "The likeness of the Sunna in this world is like the likeness of Paradise in the hereafter. Whoever enters Paradise in the hereafter is safe; likewise whoever adheres to the Sunna in this world is safe." al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "In it there is inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr); its meaning is: those whom We guided to Our path strove for Us."

﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — with victory and help in their worldly life, and with reward and forgiveness in their final abode.

﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾

Read with the yā' (ي) of "ʿibādiya" pronounced with a sukūn (إرسال الياء) by Ḥafṣ... Hmm, let me state this plainly: the yā' is pronounced without a fatḥa (إرسال الياء) according to the reading of the Iraqis, other than ʿĀṣim; the rest read it with a fatḥa.

﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي﴾

The yā' is read with a fatḥa (مفتوحة الياء) by Ibn ʿĀmir; others read it with a sukūn (ساكنة). ﴿وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾

That is, worship Me alone, without obeying any creature in disobedience to Me. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If one acts with sin in a land, then flee [in another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: leave it], for ﴿My earth is spacious﴾." [In another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAṭāʾ said: "If you are commanded to sin, then flee from it, for My earth is spacious." See the Tafsir of al-Ṭabarī: 21/12.]

Mujāhid: ﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾ means: so emigrate and strive (فهاجروا وجاهدوا).

Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: it was revealed concerning the oppressed believers who were in Mecca and could not openly display their faith or worship the Most Merciful. He urges them to emigrate and says to them: "Indeed the land of Medina is spacious and secure." Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: ﴿My earth is spacious﴾ means: My provision for you is abundant; I bring forth from the earth what is in it.

We were informed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid [in the Isfahan copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-Wazzān], who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Shādhān informed us, who said: Jīghwayh ibn Muḥammad al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr al-Nājī, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise and will be the companion of Abraham and Muhammad (peace be upon them both)." [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 5/347.] [162]

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ Therefore, do not dwell in the abode of the polytheists.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — "ghurafan" means lofty chambers (عَلالي). Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read the verb with a tāʾ (بالتاء); others read it with a yāʾ (بالياء), meaning: "He will surely settle them [in them]." ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin" means "and how many" (وكم). That is because of:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca, who had been harmed by the polytheists: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live as neighbors of the wrongdoers there." [163] [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/360.]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we leave for Medina when we have there no house, no property, and no wealth? Who will feed us there and give us drink?" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — that is, many a creature that has need of food does not carry its provision, and Allah provides for it, meaning the birds and the beasts.

﴿اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ day by day. ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, and you feared that separation from our homeland would bring poverty. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is in your hearts and of where your affairs will end.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqāq narrated to us, and he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zurāra al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl al-Jawzī [in the Isfahan copy: al-Jazarī] narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began picking dates with his hand and eating. He said: "Eat, O Ibn ʿUmar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food nor found any."

I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, if you asked your Lord, He would give me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satisfied one day. How will it be with you, O Ibn ʿUmar, when you grow old and remain among the rabble of people who hoard a year's provision and whose certainty weakens?" [Al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/149; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/359; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 3/430; and with variation in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/321.] [164] Then ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)… the verse.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, who said: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna say: "When people differ, look at what the people of the frontier (ahl al-thaghr) hold to, for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾."

al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in seeking knowledge ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْعَمَلِ بِهِ﴾ — the paths of acting upon it.

Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Aḥmad informed me, who said: Abū al-Ṭayyib Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdūn narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Jawārī narrated to us, who said: Abū Aḥmad — meaning ʿAbbās al-Hamdānī — and Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾: "Those who act upon what they know, their Lord guides them to what they do not know."

It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he spoke some words while a group of scholars was present, and al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ said to him: "By what were you given this knowledge, O Abū Marwān?" He said: "Woe to you, O Waḍīn! Our knowledge of what we did not know falls short only because of our shortcoming in acting upon what we know. If we had acted upon some of what we know, it would have bequeathed to us knowledge that our bodies could not bear."

It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "Wisdom says: whoever seeks me and does not find me, let him seek me in two places: that he act upon the best of what he knows, or that he abandon the worst of what he knows."

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي طَاعَتِنَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ ثَوَابِنَا﴾ — the paths of Our reward. Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by emigration ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الثَّبَاتِ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ﴾ — the paths of steadfastness in faith. It was also said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by steadfastness in faith ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ دُخُولِ الْجِنَانِ﴾ — the paths of entering the gardens of Paradise. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي إِقَامَةِ السُّنَّةِ لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — the paths to Paradise. Then he said: "The likeness of the Sunna in this world is like the likeness of Paradise in the hereafter. Whoever enters Paradise in the hereafter is safe; likewise whoever adheres to the Sunna in this world is safe." al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "In it there is inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr); its meaning is: those whom We guided to Our path strove for Us."

﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — with victory and help in their worldly life, and with reward and forgiveness in their final abode.

﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾

Read with the yā' (ي) of "ʿibādiya" pronounced with a sukūn (إرسال الياء) by Ḥafṣ... Hmm, let me state this plainly: the yā' is pronounced without a fatḥa (إرسال الياء) according to the reading of the Iraqis, other than ʿĀṣim; the rest read it with a fatḥa.

﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي﴾

The yā' is read with a fatḥa (مفتوحة الياء) by Ibn ʿĀmir; others read it with a sukūn (ساكنة). ﴿وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾

That is, worship Me alone, without obeying any creature in disobedience to Me. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If one acts with sin in a land, then flee [in another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: leave it], for ﴿My earth is spacious﴾." [In another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAṭāʾ said: "If you are commanded to sin, then flee from it, for My earth is spacious." See the Tafsir of al-Ṭabarī: 21/12.]

Mujāhid: ﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾ means: so emigrate and strive (فهاجروا وجاهدوا).

Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: it was revealed concerning the oppressed believers who were in Mecca and could not openly display their faith or worship the Most Merciful. He urges them to emigrate and says to them: "Indeed the land of Medina is spacious and secure." Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: ﴿My earth is spacious﴾ means: My provision for you is abundant; I bring forth from the earth what is in it.

We were informed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid [in the Isfahan copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-Wazzān], who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Shādhān informed us, who said: Jīghwayh ibn Muḥammad al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr al-Nājī, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise and will be the companion of Abraham and Muhammad (peace be upon them both)." [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 5/347.] [162]

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ Therefore, do not dwell in the abode of the polytheists.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — "ghurafan" means lofty chambers (عَلالي). Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read the verb with a tāʾ (بالتاء); others read it with a yāʾ (بالياء), meaning: "He will surely settle them [in them]." ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin" means "and how many" (وكم). That is because of:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca, who had been harmed by the polytheists: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live as neighbors of the wrongdoers there." [163] [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/360.]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we leave for Medina when we have there no house, no property, and no wealth? Who will feed us there and give us drink?" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — that is, many a creature that has need of food does not carry its provision, and Allah provides for it, meaning the birds and the beasts.

﴿اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ day by day. ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, and you feared that separation from our homeland would bring poverty. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is in your hearts and of where your affairs will end.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqāq narrated to us, and he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zurāra al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl al-Jawzī [in the Isfahan copy: al-Jazarī] narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began picking dates with his hand and eating. He said: "Eat, O Ibn ʿUmar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food nor found any."

I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, if you asked your Lord, He would give me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satisfied one day. How will it be with you, O Ibn ʿUmar, when you grow old and remain among the rabble of people who hoard a year's provision and whose certainty weakens?" [Al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/149; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/359; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 3/430; and with variation in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/321.] [164] Then ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)… the verse.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Ibn Ḥunaysh narrated to us: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAlī ibn al-Arqam [in the Isfahan copy: al-Aqmar], concerning ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾, he said: "It does not store anything for tomorrow."

Sufyān said: "Nothing that Allah has created stores up except the human being, the mouse, and the ant."

﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ. اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهَا لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ. وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ﴾ — meaning the enduring, everlasting one, which has no cessation and no death in it. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — but they do not know this.

﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ وَخَافُوا الْغَرَقَ وَالْهَلَاكَ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ. لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ — that they may deny Our favour in saving them, and the rest of the verse: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — the lām here is read with a jazm (جزم لامه) by al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf and Ayyūb; it is read variously from ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr; the rest read it with a kasra (بكسر اللام), and Abū ʿUbayd chose this, because the speech is in sequence (لكون الكلام نسقا). Whoever reads with a jazm argues from the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "yumtiʿū." ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid — concerning what he permitted me to narrate from him — who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Askat narrated to us, who said: ʿAqqāl narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Salmān narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Dīnār narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliya recite "li-yakfurū bimā ātaynāhum fa-tamattaʿū fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn" with a yāʾ. Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: ﴿My earth is spacious﴾ means: My provision for you is abundant; I bring forth from the earth what is in it.

We were informed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid [in the Isfahan copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-Wazzān], who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Shādhān informed us, who said: Jīghwayh ibn Muḥammad al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr al-Nājī, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise and will be the companion of Abraham and Muhammad (peace be upon them both)." [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 5/347.] [162]

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ Therefore, do not dwell in the abode of the polytheists.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — "ghurafan" means lofty chambers (عَلالي). Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read the verb with a tāʾ (بالتاء); others read it with a yāʾ (بالياء), meaning: "He will surely settle them [in them]." ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin" means "and how many" (وكم). That is because of:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca, who had been harmed by the polytheists: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live as neighbors of the wrongdoers there." [163] [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/360.]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we leave for Medina when we have there no house, no property, and no wealth? Who will feed us there and give us drink?" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — that is, many a creature that has need of food does not carry its provision, and Allah provides for it, meaning the birds and the beasts.

﴿اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ day by day. ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, and you feared that separation from our homeland would bring poverty. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is in your hearts and of where your affairs will end.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqāq narrated to us, and he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zurāra al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl al-Jawzī [in the Isfahan copy: al-Jazarī] narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began picking dates with his hand and eating. He said: "Eat, O Ibn ʿUmar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food nor found any."

I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, if you asked your Lord, He would give me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satisfied one day. How will it be with you, O Ibn ʿUmar, when you grow old and remain among the rabble of people who hoard a year's provision and whose certainty weakens?" [Al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/149; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/359; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 3/430; and with variation in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/321.] [164] Then ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)… the verse.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Ibn Ḥunaysh narrated to us: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAlī ibn al-Arqam [in the Isfahan copy: al-Aqmar], concerning ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾, he said: "It does not store anything for tomorrow."

Sufyān said: "Nothing that Allah has created stores up except the human being, the mouse, and the ant."

﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ. اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهَا لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ. وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ﴾ — meaning the enduring, everlasting one, which has no cessation and no death in it. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — but they do not know this.

﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ وَخَافُوا الْغَرَقَ وَالْهَلَاكَ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ. لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ — that they may deny Our favour in saving them, and the rest of the verse: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — the lām here is read with a jazm (جزم لامه) by al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf and Ayyūb; it is read variously from ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr; the rest read it with a kasra (بكسر اللام), and Abū ʿUbayd chose this, because the speech is in sequence (لكون الكلام نسقا). Whoever reads with a jazm argues from the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "yumtiʿū." ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid — concerning what he permitted me to narrate from him — who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Askat narrated to us, who said: ʿAqqāl narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Salmān narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Dīnār narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliya recite "li-yakfurū bimā ātaynāhum fa-tamattaʿū fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn" with a yāʾ. The kasra (on the lām, as in liyakfurū) is for "kay" (so that), and the jazm is for threat (التهديد).

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَمًا آمِنًا وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ أَفَبِالْبَاطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — by idols — ﴿وَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ — meaning faith. ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ — they claimed that Allah has a partner, and they said when they committed an indecency: ﴿وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَا آبَاءَنَا وَاللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا﴾ [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 28.]

﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — Muhammad and the Qur'an — ﴿لَمَّا جَاءَهُ﴾ — ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْكَافِرِينَ. وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾ — that is, those who fought for Our sake against Our enemies, for the victory of Our religion, that We may make them steadfast in what they fought for.

Abū Sūra said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in the raid (الغزو) ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سَبِيلَ الشَّهَادَةِ أَوِ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ — the path of martyrdom or forgiveness.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, who said: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna say: "When people differ, look at what the people of the frontier (ahl al-thaghr) hold to, for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾."

al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in seeking knowledge ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْعَمَلِ بِهِ﴾ — the paths of acting upon it.

Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Aḥmad informed me, who said: Abū al-Ṭayyib Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdūn narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Jawārī narrated to us, who said: Abū Aḥmad — meaning ʿAbbās al-Hamdānī — and Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾: "Those who act upon what they know, their Lord guides them to what they do not know."

It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he spoke some words while a group of scholars was present, and al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ said to him: "By what were you given this knowledge, O Abū Marwān?" He said: "Woe to you, O Waḍīn! Our knowledge of what we did not know falls short only because of our shortcoming in acting upon what we know. If we had acted upon some of what we know, it would have bequeathed to us knowledge that our bodies could not bear."

It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "Wisdom says: whoever seeks me and does not find me, let him seek me in two places: that he act upon the best of what he knows, or that he abandon the worst of what he knows."

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي طَاعَتِنَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ ثَوَابِنَا﴾ — the paths of Our reward. Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by emigration ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الثَّبَاتِ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ﴾ — the paths of steadfastness in faith. It was also said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by steadfastness in faith ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ دُخُولِ الْجِنَانِ﴾ — the paths of entering the gardens of Paradise. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي إِقَامَةِ السُّنَّةِ لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — the paths to Paradise. Then he said: "The likeness of the Sunna in this world is like the likeness of Paradise in the hereafter. Whoever enters Paradise in the hereafter is safe; likewise whoever adheres to the Sunna in this world is safe." al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "In it there is inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr); its meaning is: those whom We guided to Our path strove for Us."

﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — with victory and help in their worldly life, and with reward and forgiveness in their final abode.

﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾

Sufyān said: "Nothing that Allah has created stores up except the human being, the mouse, and the ant."

﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ. اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهَا لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ. وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ﴾ — meaning the enduring, everlasting one, which has no cessation and no death in it. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — but they do not know this.

﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ وَخَافُوا الْغَرَقَ وَالْهَلَاكَ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ. لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ — that they may deny Our favour in saving them, and the rest of the verse: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — the lām here is read with a jazm (جزم لامه) by al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf and Ayyūb; it is read variously from ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr; the rest read it with a kasra (بكسر اللام), and Abū ʿUbayd chose this, because the speech is in sequence (لكون الكلام نسقا). Whoever reads with a jazm argues from the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "yumtiʿū." ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid — concerning what he permitted me to narrate from him — who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Askat narrated to us, who said: ʿAqqāl narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Salmān narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Dīnār narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliya recite "li-yakfurū bimā ātaynāhum fa-tamattaʿū fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn" with a yāʾ. The kasra (on the lām, as in liyakfurū) is for "kay" (so that), and the jazm is for threat (التهديد).

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَمًا آمِنًا وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ أَفَبِالْبَاطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — by idols — ﴿وَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ — meaning faith. ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ — they claimed that Allah has a partner, and they said when they committed an indecency: ﴿وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَا آبَاءَنَا وَاللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا﴾ [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 28.]

﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — Muhammad and the Qur'an — ﴿لَمَّا جَاءَهُ﴾ — ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْكَافِرِينَ. وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾ — that is, those who fought for Our sake against Our enemies, for the victory of Our religion, that We may make them steadfast in what they fought for.

Abū Sūra said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in the raid (الغزو) ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سَبِيلَ الشَّهَادَةِ أَوِ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ — the path of martyrdom or forgiveness.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, who said: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna say: "When people differ, look at what the people of the frontier (ahl al-thaghr) hold to, for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾."

al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in seeking knowledge ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْعَمَلِ بِهِ﴾ — the paths of acting upon it.

Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Aḥmad informed me, who said: Abū al-Ṭayyib Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdūn narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Jawārī narrated to us, who said: Abū Aḥmad — meaning ʿAbbās al-Hamdānī — and Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾: "Those who act upon what they know, their Lord guides them to what they do not know."

It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he spoke some words while a group of scholars was present, and al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ said to him: "By what were you given this knowledge, O Abū Marwān?" He said: "Woe to you, O Waḍīn! Our knowledge of what we did not know falls short only because of our shortcoming in acting upon what we know. If we had acted upon some of what we know, it would have bequeathed to us knowledge that our bodies could not bear."

It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "Wisdom says: whoever seeks me and does not find me, let him seek me in two places: that he act upon the best of what he knows, or that he abandon the worst of what he knows."

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي طَاعَتِنَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ ثَوَابِنَا﴾ — the paths of Our reward. Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by emigration ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الثَّبَاتِ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ﴾ — the paths of steadfastness in faith. It was also said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by steadfastness in faith ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ دُخُولِ الْجِنَانِ﴾ — the paths of entering the gardens of Paradise. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي إِقَامَةِ السُّنَّةِ لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — the paths to Paradise. Then he said: "The likeness of the Sunna in this world is like the likeness of Paradise in the hereafter. Whoever enters Paradise in the hereafter is safe; likewise whoever adheres to the Sunna in this world is safe." al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "In it there is inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr); its meaning is: those whom We guided to Our path strove for Us."

﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — with victory and help in their worldly life, and with reward and forgiveness in their final abode.

﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾

Read with the yā' (ي) of "ʿibādiya" pronounced with a sukūn (إرسال الياء) by Ḥafṣ... Hmm, let me state this plainly: the yā' is pronounced without a fatḥa (إرسال الياء) according to the reading of the Iraqis, other than ʿĀṣim; the rest read it with a fatḥa.

﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي﴾

The yā' is read with a fatḥa (مفتوحة الياء) by Ibn ʿĀmir; others read it with a sukūn (ساكنة). ﴿وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾

That is, worship Me alone, without obeying any creature in disobedience to Me. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If one acts with sin in a land, then flee [in another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: leave it], for ﴿My earth is spacious﴾." [In another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAṭāʾ said: "If you are commanded to sin, then flee from it, for My earth is spacious." See the Tafsir of al-Ṭabarī: 21/12.]

Mujāhid: ﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾ means: so emigrate and strive (فهاجروا وجاهدوا).

Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: it was revealed concerning the oppressed believers who were in Mecca and could not openly display their faith or worship the Most Merciful. He urges them to emigrate and says to them: "Indeed the land of Medina is spacious and secure." Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: ﴿My earth is spacious﴾ means: My provision for you is abundant; I bring forth from the earth what is in it.

We were informed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid [in the Isfahan copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-Wazzān], who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Shādhān informed us, who said: Jīghwayh ibn Muḥammad al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr al-Nājī, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise and will be the companion of Abraham and Muhammad (peace be upon them both)." [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 5/347.] [162]

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ Therefore, do not dwell in the abode of the polytheists.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — "ghurafan" means lofty chambers (عَلالي). Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read the verb with a tāʾ (بالتاء); others read it with a yāʾ (بالياء), meaning: "He will surely settle them [in them]." ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin" means "and how many" (وكم). That is because of:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca, who had been harmed by the polytheists: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live as neighbors of the wrongdoers there." [163] [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/360.]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we leave for Medina when we have there no house, no property, and no wealth? Who will feed us there and give us drink?" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — that is, many a creature that has need of food does not carry its provision, and Allah provides for it, meaning the birds and the beasts.

﴿اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ day by day. ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, and you feared that separation from our homeland would bring poverty. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is in your hearts and of where your affairs will end.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqāq narrated to us, and he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zurāra al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl al-Jawzī [in the Isfahan copy: al-Jazarī] narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began picking dates with his hand and eating. He said: "Eat, O Ibn ʿUmar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food nor found any."

I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, if you asked your Lord, He would give me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satisfied one day. How will it be with you, O Ibn ʿUmar, when you grow old and remain among the rabble of people who hoard a year's provision and whose certainty weakens?" [Al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/149; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/359; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 3/430; and with variation in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/321.] [164] Then ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)… the verse.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, who said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, who said: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna say: "When people differ, look at what the people of the frontier (ahl al-thaghr) hold to, for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾."

al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ in seeking knowledge ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْعَمَلِ بِهِ﴾ — the paths of acting upon it.

Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Aḥmad informed me, who said: Abū al-Ṭayyib Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdūn narrated to me, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Jawārī narrated to us, who said: Abū Aḥmad — meaning ʿAbbās al-Hamdānī — and Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾: "Those who act upon what they know, their Lord guides them to what they do not know."

It is related from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that he spoke some words while a group of scholars was present, and al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ said to him: "By what were you given this knowledge, O Abū Marwān?" He said: "Woe to you, O Waḍīn! Our knowledge of what we did not know falls short only because of our shortcoming in acting upon what we know. If we had acted upon some of what we know, it would have bequeathed to us knowledge that our bodies could not bear."

It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "Wisdom says: whoever seeks me and does not find me, let him seek me in two places: that he act upon the best of what he knows, or that he abandon the worst of what he knows."

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي طَاعَتِنَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ ثَوَابِنَا﴾ — the paths of Our reward. Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by emigration ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الثَّبَاتِ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ﴾ — the paths of steadfastness in faith. It was also said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا﴾ by steadfastness in faith ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ دُخُولِ الْجِنَانِ﴾ — the paths of entering the gardens of Paradise. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِي إِقَامَةِ السُّنَّةِ لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — the paths to Paradise. Then he said: "The likeness of the Sunna in this world is like the likeness of Paradise in the hereafter. Whoever enters Paradise in the hereafter is safe; likewise whoever adheres to the Sunna in this world is safe." al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "In it there is inversion (taqdīm wa-ta'khīr); its meaning is: those whom We guided to Our path strove for Us."

﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — with victory and help in their worldly life, and with reward and forgiveness in their final abode.

﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾

Read with the yā' (ي) of "ʿibādiya" pronounced with a sukūn (إرسال الياء) by Ḥafṣ... Hmm, let me state this plainly: the yā' is pronounced without a fatḥa (إرسال الياء) according to the reading of the Iraqis, other than ʿĀṣim; the rest read it with a fatḥa.

﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي﴾

The yā' is read with a fatḥa (مفتوحة الياء) by Ibn ʿĀmir; others read it with a sukūn (ساكنة). ﴿وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾

That is, worship Me alone, without obeying any creature in disobedience to Me. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If one acts with sin in a land, then flee [in another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: leave it], for ﴿My earth is spacious﴾." [In another copy of the Isfahan manuscript: ʿAṭāʾ said: "If you are commanded to sin, then flee from it, for My earth is spacious." See the Tafsir of al-Ṭabarī: 21/12.]

Mujāhid: ﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾ means: so emigrate and strive (فهاجروا وجاهدوا).

Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: it was revealed concerning the oppressed believers who were in Mecca and could not openly display their faith or worship the Most Merciful. He urges them to emigrate and says to them: "Indeed the land of Medina is spacious and secure." Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: ﴿My earth is spacious﴾ means: My provision for you is abundant; I bring forth from the earth what is in it.

We were informed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid [in the Isfahan copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-Wazzān], who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Shādhān informed us, who said: Jīghwayh ibn Muḥammad al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, who said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr al-Nājī, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise and will be the companion of Abraham and Muhammad (peace be upon them both)." [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 5/347.] [162]

﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ Therefore, do not dwell in the abode of the polytheists.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — "ghurafan" means lofty chambers (عَلالي). Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read the verb with a tāʾ (بالتاء); others read it with a yāʾ (بالياء), meaning: "He will surely settle them [in them]." ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — "wa-ka'ayyin" means "and how many" (وكم). That is because of:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca, who had been harmed by the polytheists: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live as neighbors of the wrongdoers there." [163] [Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/360.]

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can we leave for Medina when we have there no house, no property, and no wealth? Who will feed us there and give us drink?" So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ — that is, many a creature that has need of food does not carry its provision, and Allah provides for it, meaning the birds and the beasts.

﴿اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ day by day. ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, and you feared that separation from our homeland would bring poverty. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of what is in your hearts and of where your affairs will end.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Raqqāq narrated to us, and he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zurāra al-Raqqī narrated to us, who said: Abū al-ʿAṭūf al-Jarrāḥ ibn al-Minhāl al-Jawzī [in the Isfahan copy: al-Jazarī] narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a garden of the gardens of the Anṣār, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began picking dates with his hand and eating. He said: "Eat, O Ibn ʿUmar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food nor found any."

I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn ʿUmar, if you asked your Lord, He would give me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satisfied one day. How will it be with you, O Ibn ʿUmar, when you grow old and remain among the rabble of people who hoard a year's provision and whose certainty weakens?" [Al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/149; Tafsir al-Qurṭubī: 13/359; Tafsir Ibn Kathīr: 3/430; and with variation in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/321.] [164] Then ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)… the verse.

We were informed by Ibn Fanjawayh: Ibn Ḥunaysh narrated to us: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAlī ibn al-Arqam [in the Isfahan copy: al-Aqmar], concerning ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾, he said: "It does not store anything for tomorrow."

Sufyān said: "Nothing that Allah has created stores up except the human being, the mouse, and the ant."

﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ. اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهَا لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ. وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ﴾ — meaning the enduring, everlasting one, which has no cessation and no death in it. ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — but they do not know this.

﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ وَخَافُوا الْغَرَقَ وَالْهَلَاكَ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ. لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ — that they may deny Our favour in saving them, and the rest of the verse: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — the lām here is read with a jazm (جزم لامه) by al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf and Ayyūb; it is read variously from ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr; the rest read it with a kasra (بكسر اللام), and Abū ʿUbayd chose this, because the speech is in sequence (لكون الكلام نسقا). Whoever reads with a jazm argues from the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "yumtiʿū." ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid — concerning what he permitted me to narrate from him — who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Saʿīd informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Askat narrated to us, who said: ʿAqqāl narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Salmān narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Dīnār narrated to us, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliya recite "li-yakfurū bimā ātaynāhum fa-tamattaʿū fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn" with a yāʾ. The kasra (on the lām, as in liyakfurū) is for "kay" (so that), and the jazm is for threat (التهديد).

﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا حَرَمًا آمِنًا وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ أَفَبِالْبَاطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — by idols — ﴿وَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ — meaning faith. ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ — they claimed that Allah has a partner, and they said when they committed an indecency: ﴿وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَا آبَاءَنَا وَاللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا﴾ [Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 28.]
